STATE.md

STATE — read this first after any restart/compaction

Goal (from user, 2026-10-21)

Build a fast, non-graphical osu!standard (osu! ruleset only; no taiko/mania/catch) replay evaluator that is

*exactly* equivalent to osu!lazer's judgment/scoring: given .osu beatmap + .osr replay + mods (with mod settings),

output identical judgments, statistics, max combo, accuracy, total score, pass/fail.

  • Lazer is the absolute source of truth. Pin one release (latest tag as of start).
  • Ignore osu!stable's evaluation scheme (stable-set scores have different judgement). Only lazer logic.
  • Must support ALL lazer osu! mods + combinations + mod settings (DT/HT rates, DA, etc.).
  • Approach: (1) extract formal model (Lean 4) of lazer's evaluation; (2) gain extreme confidence model == lazer

    • (differential testing vs headless lazer on real replays from osu! API + fuzzed/PBT replays; formal where possible);

    (3) efficient Rust implementation proven to refine the model (Verus or alternative after research).

  • Ratchet: simplest end-to-end round trip first (NoMod, circles only), then add sliders, spinners, mods...
  • User is away for a long time; no further interaction. Make reasonable choices, log in DECISIONS.md.

Environment

  • VM (since 2026-10-21 reboot): 4 vCPU, 7.7GB RAM, 6GB swap (/swapfile 2G + /swapfile2 4G added 2026-10-22, both in fstab), 50GB disk total (grown 2026-10-21, resize2fs), ~27GB free (disk is the scarcest resource! lean toolchain 3GB, nuget 1.4GB). Root via sudo allowed, anything allowed.
  • osu! API v1 key + v2 OAuth client (OSU_API_V2_CLIENT_ID/SECRET, client_credentials, scope public: lazer replay

    • download works) in ~/.osu_credentials. NEVER commit it. Pulling tens of thousands of replays is OK

    (respect rate limits: get_replay ~10/min).

  • Project repo: ~/lazerproof (local git, commit often, no remote).
  • Small machine: avoid running multiple heavy builds (dotnet / lake / cargo) concurrently.

SAFETY RULES for all agents (include in every subagent prompt)

  • Never rm with a variable/glob that could expand to $HOME (e.g. rm -rf $X/*). Only delete literal absolute paths

    • inside ~/lazerproof/<subdir> or the scratchpad. Prefer lake clean/dotnet clean/cargo clean.

  • earlyoom installed (/etc/default/earlyoom): kills largest process at <=8% mem & <=15% swap; prefers aeneas/charon/dotnet/oracle/bm*/simtest*/evaltest/osu_eval/cargo/rustc (batch, restartable), NOT lean (the shared proof REPL), avoids claude/python3 (D32).
  • MODELLING RULE: model code is translated from the lazer/osu-framework SOURCE (cite file:line), never from docs/*.md

    • summaries (docs are maps; e.g. lazer-map once had a wrong float grouping in DifficultyRange -> 1-ulp health bug).

  • HEAVY JOBS — CHUNK RULE: never wrap a long multi-step script in ONE tools/heavy call; wrap each step (<= ~15 min) separately so builds can interleave (the semaphore is not fair).
  • HEAVY JOBS (exclusive: HEAVY_EXCLUSIVE=1 tools/heavy takes the whole machine, for Aeneas ~2.9GB; use sparingly): wrap every CPU/memory-heavy command in tools/heavy <cmd> (machine-wide 3-slot semaphore + waits for

    • >=900MB MemAvailable; nested calls pass through). oracle/oracle.sh already does this and transparently caches batch

    results (tools/oracle_cache.py, data/oracle-cache, keyed by dll+file hashes+options; ORACLE_NOCACHE=1 bypasses).

    Use it for: lake build, cargo build, bmtest/bmdump/simtest batches, dotnet build.

  • MEMORY BUDGET: 7.7GB RAM total, shared. No single process > ~2GB (Aeneas: use HEAVY_EXCLUSIVE). For dotnet batch tools set

    • DOTNET_GCHeapHardLimit=0x30000000 and run long batches in chunks (restart process every <=200 jobs).

  • status/diskguard.sh (cron 5min) SIGSTOPs fetch_v1/v2 when free disk < 2.5GB, SIGCONTs > 3.5GB.
  • After any dotnet build run tools/prune_runtimes.sh <outdir> (saves ~340MB per output dir).
  • status/scratch_janitor.sh (cron hourly) deletes scratch dirs idle >6h with no open files. Keep your scratch < 300MB.
  • DISK BUDGET: keep >=8GB free (df -h /). Delete your own scratch outputs when done (literal paths). Don't create new

    • .NET projects that rebuild lazer (each costs ~650MB) — reuse oracle/ (add commands/flags) or model/bmtest.

  • Never touch ~/.osu_credentials contents in output/commits; never push anywhere yourself. (The user set up a LOCAL private

    • Forgejo mirror, https://osu-judgments.exe.xyz:3000/osu/lazerproof; .git/hooks/post-commit + cron push to it via

    tools/forgejo/sync.sh. So: never commit secrets, since everything committed is mirrored there.)

DECISIONS.md

Decisions log (made autonomously; user away)

  • D1: Lazer version = latest tagged release at project start; commit pinned in LAZER_COMMIT.
  • D2: "Result" = per-object judgements (HitResult incl. ticks/slider ends/bonus), statistics counts, max combo,

    • accuracy, standardised total score, pass/fail (with mods like SD/PF/fail). No pp/star rating.

  • D3: Oracle = lazer's own code driven headlessly (no rendering), validated against real lazer play-back semantics.

    • Real scores' server stats used as an additional check where available.

  • D4: Repo local only, never pushed.
  • D5: Non-provable parts (float-heavy path math, RNG mods) are modelled faithfully (bit-exact IEEE semantics) and

    • covered by exhaustive differential testing; gaps documented, never silently simplified.

  • D6 (tentative, see docs/verification-tools.md): Spec in Lean 4 (kernel-reducible Float since 4.33; we define

    • .NET-semantics floor/ceil/round-half-even/f64<->f32 ourselves via bits). Rust impl proven against spec via

    Charon/Aeneas; floats via thin F32/F64 bit-wrapper types with trusted, exhaustively tested primitives.

    Transcendentals (pow/atan2/sin/cos/acos) are trusted primitives sharing glibc with .NET; pin glibc version.

    Lean model is natively compiled and itself diff-tested vs lazer early (and is a fallback evaluator).

  • D7: Ground truth = lazer headless playback result of the replay, NOT the server-stored stats (live score can

    • differ from replay playback). Server stats used only as a sanity signal.

  • D8: Disk is tight (~9GB free). Mathlib/Aeneas install deferred until spec+impl exist; keep replay corpus

    • compressed and bounded.

  • D9: Lazer's judgement depends on the FrameStabilityContainer step schedule (framerate-dependent in real play).

    • The model + impl take the *reference-clock trajectory* (hence the step-time schedule) as an explicit input, so

    equivalence holds for every schedule. Canonical schedule for scoring ("the" result): fixed far target, i.e.

    t_{k+1} = SetFrame(next replay frame, or t_k + 1000/60 if gap > 1.2f*1000/60) — what lazer does when catching up /

    fast-forwarding. Oracle also runs per-frame and dense-1ms schedules to measure schedule sensitivity.

  • D10: Fixed environment: 1024x768 window, UI scale 1, default config (IncreaseFirstObjectVisibility=true, snaking on),

    • default skin. Hit tests replicate the float32 screen-space pipeline for this environment.

  • D11: Pass/fail reported with live-Player semantics (fail freezes score at failing judgement, respecting fail overrides);

    • ReplayPlayer semantics also reported.

  • D12 (see docs/proof-pipeline.md): Proof route = Rust impl translated by Charon/Aeneas (prebuilt release bundle) with a

    • *filtered* Mathlib cache (only modules Aeneas imports; ~2.5GB total), proven to refine the Lean spec. Started only once

    the spec reaches M4 and disk allows. Fallback (if disk/Aeneas blocks): optimised Lean evaluator proven equal to the

    clear spec (no Mathlib), Rust as thin FFI shell. Spec code should follow the Lean perf rules in proof-pipeline.md

    where cheap (it is compiled and diff-tested at scale).

  • D13: v1 replays are osu!stable scores; their server stats come from STABLE judgement, so oracle-vs-server mismatches

    • there reflect lazer(+Classic) != stable, not model errors. The meaningful real-world check is LAZER scores (API v2

    /scores/{id}/download, scope public) vs their server stats: expect near-total agreement, with residual differences only

    in schedule-sensitive judgements (lazer records replays at <=60fps: ReplayRecorder.cs:33,80; live play samples every

    frame). Any non-schedule-sensitive mismatch there = our mental model is wrong. Requested v2 client creds from user.

  • D14: D12 confirmed by POC (docs/proof-poc.md). Order: Rust port mirrors Lean defs 1:1 and is diff-tested vs Lean

    • executables first (cheap); refinement proofs follow per module.

  • D13a (2026-10-21, server-agreement agent): after the disk grew to 50 GB the v2 lazer-score crawl bound was raised

    • 5000 -> 8000 (crawl_v2_watchdog.sh; ~60 KB/score incl. .osu) and its stop threshold to 10 GB free (budget >= 8 GB).

    Triage (difftest/triage_v2.py) now defaults to pinned sim/evaltest copies in data/oracle_v2/pinned/ because other

    agents relink the live binaries; every triage run is still gated against the oracle's catchup result.

  • D15 (G17): The Lean sim is total, with Except String as the rejection channel. Fuel exhaustion and internal invariant violations

    • reject the input instead of truncating or returning a default. Wherever lazer itself throws (Math.Clamp with min>max, Math.Sign(NaN),

    Path.Vertices[0] on an empty path, invalid Period), the model rejects with lazer would throw, consistent with G12. The mods-JSON

    reader stays partial (input parsing, no panics).

  • D16 (2026-10-21, Rust sim port): the Rust port of the total sim (D15, Lean e0e8215) returns Result<_, SimErr> from every

    • function through which a spec rejection is reachable; SimErr has one variant per spec throw site and simtest_rs

    renders the spec's exact message, so rejections are diff-tested byte for byte. The spec's `internal: index … out of

    range accessors (getA/setA/need on invariant-sized arrays) stay Rust indexing (panic = Aeneas fail`): they are

    unreachable, and refinement only needs "spec .ok => same in-range accesses". The proof-POC crate::schedule keeps

    the pre-G17 simulateSteps (its proof targets a frozen spec copy); the sim uses a rejecting copy in sim::schedule.

  • D17 (2026-10-21, refinement proofs): proof iteration uses a long-lived file-driven Lean REPL (proofs/scripts/Repl.lean,

    • ~1.6 GB RSS, idle most of the time) started with nice *outside* tools/heavy: holding a heavy slot for hours would

    starve other agents, and waiting for a slot starved the REPL (the semaphore is not fair). Every real build/audit

    (lake build, check_all.sh) still runs under tools/heavy. Refinement theorems over strings assume ValidStr

    (Unicode scalar values) and size bounds like len < 2^62; such guards are stated in the theorem, never assumed silently.

  • D18 (2026-10-22, Rust end-to-end port): impl/osu_eval_core/src/eval/ ports Eval.lean, Eval/Adapter.lean, Eval/Env.lean,

    • Replay/Osr.lean and Sim/ModsJson.lean (the JSON reader Osr and --mods depend on) into one new module tree, rather than

    adding files to the sim port's sim//replay/ (other agents' areas). LZMA stays the trusted boundary: crate::lzma

    (opaque to Charon) is a line-by-line port of model/c/lzma_shim.c calling the same system liblzma 5.4.5 via

    dlopen("liblzma.so.5") (no build script, no new link dependency for simtest_rs/bmdump_rs; Lean links the static

    liblzma.a of the same package). Spec String messages are error enums with payload ids; texts live in untranslated

    text submodules (as beatmap::errors::text). Printing mirrors the Lean runtime, which canonicalises NaN in

    Float.toBits (checked: 0x7ff8000000000000 / 0x7fc00000); osu_eval prints NaNs canonically. Not ported: the

    spec's debugging option playableOverride (--sim-playable).

  • D19 (2026-10-22, refinement proofs): the proof REPL runs inside systemd-run --user --scope -p MemoryMax=2800M (it

    • sits at ~2.4-2.6 GB with Mathlib+Aeneas+OsuProofs loaded; a few elaboration requests - omega over large contexts -

    grew to 6 GB and earlyoom killed the REPL, which could equally have hit another agent's job). The cap confines such

    runaways to the REPL. Risky proofs are first checked as standalone lake env lean runs under the same kind of cap.

    Decimal refinement theorems are guarded by decimal validity (mantissa < 2^96, scale <= 28); the chained callers

    (BindableNumber snapping) discharge the guards with spec-level validity lemmas (DecimalValid.lean), so no guard

    surfaces at the framework/mod-settings level.

  • D20 (2026-10-22, orchestrator; user-approved) — Proofs are the critical path; machine time reprioritised.

    • Meta review: proof throughput fell from ~95 to ~6 fns/h, all proofs hand-written (no @[progress] automation), and one

    Lean proof process costs ~4 GB (2.3 GB private), so proofs could not be parallelised. Decisions:

    (a) server-agreement oracle loop + triage backlog PAUSED (data/oracle_v2/STOP); eval coverage loop at nice 19;

    the lazer-coverage agent continues (targets unexercised branches).

    request is cancelled. (c) Repeat offenders: culprit twice within 60 min -> its client env is dropped automatically

    (watchdog_dropped.*, note in the .out). (d) A stale drop file in an unserved client dir is consumed at scan time

Docs

docs/data-sources.md

Data sources for differential testing (replays + beatmaps)

Researched 2026-10-21 using docs plus a few small live calls. The API key is in ~/.osu_credentials

(OSU_API_V1_KEY). It is never written into the repo or into logs.

TL;DR

  • Real stable replays: osu! API v1 get_replay works with our key. It returns only the base64 LZMA

    • frame stream, and difftest/fetch_v1.py rebuilds full .osr files from it. The rate limit is 10/min,

    so about 14k replays/day.

  • v1 has only osu!stable scores. No lazer-set scores appear in get_scores, get_user_best or

    • get_user_recent, and get_replay on a lazer score id returns {"error":"Replay not available."}.

    Lazer reads stable replays as legacy scores and adds the Classic mod (LegacyScoreDecoder:

    version < 30000000 ⇒ +CL). Their server stats are stable judgements, so they are a sanity check

    only and must not be treated as the oracle. The oracle is headless lazer run on the replay.

  • Lazer replays need v2 GET /api/v2/scores/{id}/download with an OAuth token. We have no v2

    • credentials. Unauthenticated requests return 403 (api/v2) or 401 (web route). Untested option: a

    client-credentials token from an OAuth app registered in account settings would probably work, since

    the controller code allows API requests without a user.

  • Beatmaps: https://osu.ppy.sh/osu/{beatmap_id} returns raw .osu text with no auth. We can also

    • bulk download data.ppy.sh/YYYY_MM_DD_osu_files.tar.bz2 (about 1.4 GB, all ranked/loved .osu).

  • data.ppy.sh dumps contain no replays. They are MySQL table dumps only (see below).

osu! API v1 (https://github.com/ppy/osu-api/wiki)

Global documented limit: "1200 requests per minute, with a burst capability of up to 200 beyond that".

No rate-limit headers are returned (checked: none in the response headers).

| endpoint | key params | notes |

|---|---|---|

| get_beatmaps | since (MySQL date, ranked-date ≥), s, b, u, m, a (include converts, default 0), h (md5), mods, limit ≤ 500 | gives file_md5, difficultyrating, count_normal/slider/spinner, hit_length, max_combo, approved (1 ranked, 2 approved, 3 qualified, 4 loved) |

| get_scores | b (required), u, m, mods (exact enabled_mods match), type, limit ≤ 100 | fields: score_id, score, username, user_id, maxcombo, count50/100/300, countmiss, countkatu, countgeki, perfect, enabled_mods, date, rank, pp, replay_available |

| get_user_best | u, m, type, limit ≤ 100 | same score fields plus beatmap_id; stable only |

| get_user_recent | u, m, type, limit ≤ 50 | last 24h; stable only (it was empty for a lazer-only player) |

| get_replay | s = score_id (or b+u[+mods]), m, type | 10 requests/minute; "not intended for batch retrievals". Returns {"content": <base64>, "encoding": "base64"} or {"error":"Replay not available."} |

Observations from the live calls:

  • get_replay content is the raw LZMA-alone stream: 5 property bytes, then int64 uncompressed size,

    • then compressed data. Python can read it with lzma.decompress(..., format=lzma.FORMAT_ALONE). The

    decompressed text is w|x|y|keys, frames ending in the -12345|0|0|<rng seed> frame. There is no .osr header.

  • replay_available was 1 for nearly all top-50 scores we sampled (top 50/100 boards). Some

    • mod-filtered results had 0.

  • v1 score_id is the *legacy* stable id. The public web page https://osu.ppy.sh/scores/osu/{legacy_id}

    • (no auth) embeds json-show with the solo-score id, legacy_score_id, lazer-converted statistics

    (e.g. {"great":1982,"ok":1}), maximum_statistics, mods incl. CL, and standardised total_score.

    These numbers are converted from the stats, not replayed, but they are useful as a second check.

  • The web endpoint https://osu.ppy.sh/beatmaps/{id}/scores?mode=osu (no auth, JSON) lists the top 50

    • including lazer scores (build_id set, legacy_score_id null) with full lazer statistics

    (slider_tail_hit, large_tick_hit, small_bonus, ignore_hit, ...). These are the exact targets

    for our evaluator, but their replays need v2 auth.

Reconstructing a full .osr (as done in fetch_v1.py::build_osr)

Field order matches osu.Game/Scoring/Legacy/LegacyScoreDecoder.cs. All values are little-endian.

A string is 0x0b + ULEB128 length + UTF-8, or 0x00 for null.

| field | type | source |

|---|---|---|

| mode | byte | 0 |

| version | int32 | not in v1. We use the play date yyyymmdd, clamped ≥ 20140721. It must stay < 30000000 so lazer treats the replay as legacy (+CL). |

| beatmap md5 | string | get_beatmaps.file_md5. Lazer looks the beatmap up by this hash, so it must equal the md5 of the .osu we downloaded. The script checks it (osu_status). |

| player | string | username |

| replay md5 | string | not available. Lazer ignores it, so we write an approximation of stable's recipe. |

| n300, n100, n50, geki, katu, miss | uint16 ×6 | count300/100/50/countgeki/countkatu/countmiss |

| score | int32 | score |

| max combo | uint16 | maxcombo |

| perfect | bool | perfect |

| mods | int32 | enabled_mods |

| life bar | string | empty (not available) |

| timestamp | int64 .NET ticks | date, treated as UTC (unverified, but irrelevant for judging) |

| replay data | int32 len + bytes | decoded get_replay content, as is |

| online score id | int64 (version ≥ 20140721) | score_id |

Old stable files can carry trailing bytes, which lazer ignores. Note that for beatmap file version < 5,

lazer applies EARLY_VERSION_TIMING_OFFSET (+24 ms) to frames.

Beatmap files

  • https://osu.ppy.sh/osu/{beatmap_id} returns text/plain with content-disposition: attachment. It

    • needs no auth and returns no rate-limit headers. There is no documented limit; the script uses

    1 request/s. The md5 of the download matched file_md5 in every sampled case.

  • data.ppy.sh *_osu_files.tar.bz2 (2026_09_01: 1.43 GB) holds all ranked/approved/loved .osu

    • files. Use it for a large crawl so we don't hit /osu/ thousands of times.

data.ppy.sh dumps (https://data.ppy.sh, licence: statistical analysis/testing only, no redistribution)

Monthly YYYY_MM_DD_performance_{osu,taiko,catch,mania}_{top_1000,top_10000,random_10000}.tar.bz2

(osu top_1000 is about 1.3 GB, top_10000 about 5.5 GB) and *_osu_files.tar.bz2. The full listing of

2026_09_01_performance_taiko_top_1000 (layout is identical across rulesets) has 13 SQL files:

osu_beatmap_difficulty(_attribs), osu_beatmap_failtimes, osu_beatmap_performance_blacklist,

osu_beatmaps, osu_beatmapsets, osu_counts, osu_difficulty_attribs, osu_scores_<mode>_high

(stable high scores), osu_user_beatmap_playcount, osu_user_stats_<mode>, sample_users, scores

(lazer scores table: data JSON with statistics, maximum_statistics, mods incl. settings; plus

legacy_score_id, has_replay, build_id).

No replay files are included. The scores table is still valuable. It gives (score id → lazer

statistics/mods) for top players, including lazer scores, and could drive a v2 download if we ever get

credentials.

Other public replay sources

  • circleguard/circlecore tests/resources/ (GitHub): about 511 osu!std .osr (legit 88+53,

    • stealing 306, timewarped 39, relax 5, auto/cursordance 15, ...). Mostly stable with the beatmap ids in

    the names. Good for edge cases such as timewarp (frame-time manipulation) and auto/cursordance (perfect

    plays). Beatmaps must be fetched separately by md5 (get_beatmaps?h=).

  • kszlim/osu-replay-parser tests/resources/: 7 files, including lazer_standard_format.osr

    • (lazer v30000000, osu!std), replay.osr (Cookiezi FREEDOM DiVE, v20140226) and an old replay-id format.

  • No Kaggle or HuggingFace osu! replay dataset turned up in a quick search.
  • Lazer repo (lazer/, pinned): no osu!std .osr. There are only

    • `osu.Game.Tests/Resources/Replays/{taiko-replay, taiko-replay-with-legacy-online-id,

    taiko-replay-with-new-online-id, mania-replay}.osr`. The osu! ruleset tests build replays in code

    (TestSceneLegacyHitPolicy, TestSceneLegacyReplayPlayback, TestSceneSliderInput etc. use

    frame lists, which is a good source of hand-crafted edge cases). The .osu test files are:

  • osu.Game.Rulesets.Osu.Tests/Resources/Testing/Beatmaps/: `basic, colinear-perfect-curve,

    • diffcalc-test, multi-segment-slider, nan-slider, old-stacking, repeat-slider, slider-paths-edge-case,

    slider-ticks, slider-ticks-edge-case, uneven-repeat-slider, very-fast-slider, zero-length-sliders,

    801165, 1124896, 1341554, 2593923 (most have *-expected-conversion.json`)

  • osu.Game.Rulesets.Osu.Tests/Resources/SampleLookups/osu-hitobject-beatmap-custom-sample-bank.osu
  • osu.Game.Tests/Resources/*.osu (about 45 decoder tests, e.g. Soleily - Renatus (Gamu) [Insane].osu,

    • Within Temptation - The Unforgiving (Armin) [Marathon].osu, beatmap-version-4.osu,

docs/fidelity-evidence.md

Fidelity evidence: "Lean model = osu!lazer" (2026-10-23, fidelity reviewer, D68)

The refinement proofs establish Rust = Lean spec. Whether the Lean spec = lazer (pinned 2026.1005.0-lazer =

ppy/osu 9a10d935b0, osu-framework 2026.921.1, .NET 10.0.13, glibc 2.39, env D10) holds rests only on empirical

evidence. This file collects that evidence, says how current it is, lists the gaps and ranks the next checks.

Read-only review: the spec was not edited.

There are three different claims, and they must not be mixed up:

| claim | meaning | measured by |

|---|---|---|

| (A) model = harness | Lean/Rust output equals the headless oracle (lazer's own code in oracle/) for the same inputs, schedule and env | differential tests (nettest, bmtest, sim_diff, eval_diff, covfuzz) |

| (B) harness = lazer playback | the oracle's wiring (Gameplay.cs mirrors Player/ReplayPlayer; own clock, StubPlayer, fail logic, deterministic schedules) behaves like lazer's real ReplayPlayer | oracle player validation (real ReplayPlayer, recorded step list fed back as explicit:), oracle step_check |

| (C) playback = live client | replaying the .osr gives the stats the live client submitted | server agreement (D13). It measures (B)+(C) together. The model is not involved at all |

"Lean = lazer" in the project's sense (D7: ground truth = lazer replay playback) is (A) ∘ (B). (C) is a sanity

signal: it can expose a (B) bug, but most of its mismatches are inherent (60 fps / integer-ms replays, schedule D9).

2. Gaps

2.1 Weak or missing comparisons (claim A)

  • Explicit / irregular schedules are never diff-tested. D9 claims equivalence "for every schedule". The model

    • implements Schedule.explicit (Eval.lean:34, simulateSteps), but no harness (eval_diff, sim_diff,

    rust_*_diff, covfuzz) ever ran it against the oracle. Every comparison uses catchup, perframe or dense1ms:

    integer or frame-aligned references with no duplicate entries. Not covered: fractional sub-ms references,

    repeated equal references (an extra step at the same time), references between frames below 1 ms, long jumps

    (> 1.2*16.67 catch-up splitting with odd remainders), schedules that stop before the end (completed=false).

    A real-time ReplayPlayer and live play produce exactly such schedules. The oracle side is validated by its

    step_check against the real FSC. The model's simulateSteps is a transcription of oracle/Schedule.cs that

    is tested only on the three regular kinds.

  • dense1ms on real lazer replays. It is the schedule closest to live play (it fixes 12/25 server mismatches),

    • but model-vs-oracle dense1ms is mostly synthetic: covfuzz 400, M5/M6/M7 pools 12-17 jobs, 20 stable M4,

    10 stable own mods. There are essentially no lazer-v2 dense1ms comparisons (1 cached oracle job).

  • M7 / rare mods on real play. Real lazer v2 scores in the 8000-score corpus: GR 8, DF 4, SI 4, WG 4, TR 2,

    • RP 2, MG 5, DP 17, BR 17, TP 1, WD 2, WU 14, FR 8. The M7 evidence is mostly 40 synthetic maps per mod plus

    stable replays played *with mods they were not recorded with*. Those replays do not chase moved or scaled

    objects, so the hit and tracking paths under transformed geometry are exercised far less than the miss paths.

    The sensitivity counts in model-sim.md (e.g. GR 22/40, DF 13/22, TP 23/40) show that the effect is visible but

    not dense.

  • Settings value coverage.
  • modgen_sim.py never generates DA extended_limits (it does generate AR -10..11, but these clamp without the

    • flag). Only bmtest (beatmap side) and 94 real v2 scores exercise extended DA, e.g. AR > 10 preempt, OD > 10

    windows, CS > 10 radius.

  • The sim generator draws a mod set without duplicates (rng.sample). Duplicate mods (lazer applies any list)

    • are tested only beatmap-side.

  • Range extremes appear only at the generator's ~10% "edge" rate (DT/HT 2.0/0.5, WU/WD/AS endpoints, DF 25,

    • GR 0, BR 12, AC 0.999).

  • D21 notes that value coverage, unlike branch coverage, was never measured.
  • Stable replay corpus. 4490 stable replays exist; about 300-600 were compared end-to-end. This is the only

    • corpus where the legacy Relax Update runs (RX is a no-op on lazer replays), along with Classic note-lock,

    legacy health and stable frame fixups on real play.

  • Fail semantics on real fails. The feed has only passed scores (G10). Fail paths are compared only on

    • synthetic jobs, random fail mods on real replays (M5fail 30 perframe, M4, covfuzz onejudgement) and NF jobs

    that trigger failure (890 ReplayPlayer re-runs above).

  • The ~580 earliest v2 scores were never compared end-to-end. Their oracle cache entries predate the oracle

    • fingerprint change (a0244b1) and the coverage loop stopped at 10-22 06:21. They include **8 of the 51

    server-suspicious ids**: 7737710092, 7737744394, 7737756477, 7737759694, 7737822303, 7737832649, 7737873103,

  • Some of these were validated per judgement by the tracking-trace tooling (sim level, 8 scores).
  • Oracle OOMs. 5 lazer scores have no lazer result because the oracle runs under

    • DOTNET_GCHeapHardLimit (768 MB): 7738634568, 7738634727, 7738635629, 7737901342, 7737901269. This is a

    harness artefact; the real client has no such cap. The model gives a result on them that nobody has checked.

  • Malformed inputs. Model-vs-lazer behaviour on corrupt .osr/.osu rests on 14 hand-made .osr cases and the

    • bmtest fuzz. The 7k-run .osr fuzz compared Rust with Lean only.

  • Bezier subdivision fuel truncates silently (final-audit m9). bSplineToPiecewiseLinear

    • (Beatmap/PathApproximator.lean:111) runs for _ in [0:100000000] and, when the fuel runs out, emits the

    truncated output plus the last point. Every other fuel loop rejects. lazer has no bound

    (osu-framework PathApproximator.cs:105-140).

  • Reachability. Coordinates are bounded: Parsing.MAX_COORDINATE_VALUE = 131072

    • (ConvertHitObjectParser.cs:58,344), and paths are relative to the head, so |coord| < 2^18. Each de Casteljau

    halving divides the control polygon's second differences by ≥ 4, i.e. the flatness measure (squared length,

    threshold 0.25) by ≥ 16. From ≤ 2·(2^20)^2 = 2^41 that takes ≤ 11 levels, which is ≤ ~4,100 iterations per

    Bezier piece. float32 rounding noise at |x| ≤ 2^18 (ulp 2^-5) is far below the tolerance, so subdivision

    cannot stall.

  • Plain B| sliders (one Bezier of degree n-1 per segment) therefore stay ≤ ~4,100 iterations per call,

    • however many points they have.

  • The fuel can only run out for an explicit-degree B-spline segment (B2|, B3|, ...,

    • ConvertHitObjectParser.cs:245-247). That needs ≳ 25k-50k control points in a single segment with

    near-maximal zigzag (a ~0.5 MB line), or ≳ 10^8 points at degree 1.

  • No ranked map comes close. Only a crafted or fuzzed map could reach it. On such a map lazer itself spends

    • > 10^8 subdivision steps and hundreds of MB of output, so in the game it would most likely hit the 10 s

    GetPlayableBeatmap timeout or OOM.

  • Classification: a fidelity gap of the G12 kind (input on which lazer fails or is resource-bound). The

    • model silently gives a result with a truncated path, which violates D15's "fuel exhaustion rejects".

  • Recommended fix: reject. Set a flag when the loop finishes with toFlatten non-empty, return

    • Except/stage "playable" ("path approximation fuel exhausted"), mirror it in Rust, and patch the beatmap

    proof (bspline_to_piecewise_linear refinement). This is behaviour-preserving on every input that does not

    exhaust the fuel, so a D20(c) provability/totality fix.

  • Alternative: prove the fuel unreachable under a size bound (control points per segment < ~2·10^4) added to

    • PlayableBounds/InputBounds. That requires a float contraction proof, which is much harder. Either way,

    record the bound in proof-pipeline §5.

| Fail-gate deviation | the oracle's ReplayPlayer fail gate uses frame-stable time instead of GameplayClockContainer.CurrentTime (oracle README "Deviations") | the model copies the harness: a known (B) deviation, only for ReplayPlayer semantics. Live semantics unaffected |

3. "model ≠ lazer" vs "harness ≠ real client"

  • (A) model ≠ harness. No open case. 0 mismatches on every comparison since the eval env fix (95499c3):

    • about 20k end-to-end jobs (10.6M judgements in today's re-run alone), plus ~19k beatmaps and ~10^8 float checks. The

    weaknesses are coverage gaps (§2.1), not observed differences.

  • (B) harness ≠ lazer's real ReplayPlayer. This is the weakest link, and nothing else measures it.
  • The harness re-wires Player.load/LoadComplete by hand: processors, mod application order, StubPlayer for

    • IApplicableToPlayer, its own IGameplayClock, fail handling, disabled samples, no storyboard or beatmap

    skin, deterministic schedules.

  • The only check against lazer's real ReplayPlayer (oracle player: record its steps, replay them as

    • explicit:, require identical judgements) ran on 9 replays: 5 stable HD/HR/DT/NC/FL and 2 stable + 2

    lazer at the R2R swap, all on 10-21.

  • None had M6/M7/rate-ramp/AS/fail mods, which were added afterwards and whose wiring (P3 playfield updates, AP

    • cursor injection, input interceptors, IApplicableToPlayer, health-processor choice, fail overrides) is exactly

    where the harness could deviate.

  • The oracle's step_check validates only the schedule re-implementation, not the wiring.
  • Server agreement can expose (B) bugs only indirectly, mixed with (C) noise.
  • (C) playback ≠ live client. Server agreement measures this: 63.0% exact on catchup, ~99% exact or

    • schedule-explained by heuristic, 0.86% suspicious. It also differs from the D10 environment:

  • Screen and skin. Hit tests depend on the 1024x768 float32 screen-space chain, UI scale and the skin's

    • slider path radius (G4). Users play at other resolutions and skins, so playback on their machine can differ at

    the rounding level.

  • Platform libm. Class A includes Windows/macOS/Android builds. Their Math.Sin/Cos/Atan2/Pow come from

    • the Windows CRT, Apple libm or bionic, not glibc 2.39 (perfect-curve arcs, spinner atan2f, BR rotation,

    easing). The pinned glibc makes the model = linux-x64 lazer by definition. Another platform's lazer can differ

    by an ulp.

  • Live input. Live input is sampled every frame (often 1000 Hz and above). The replay keeps ≤ 60 fps,

    • integer-ms frames.

None of these is a model error, and server agreement cannot separate them from a (B) bug. That is why

validating (B) directly (check #1 below) is worth more than more server triage.

Real-Player fail path: blocked by the harness tooling, not run. 7739431096 (CL; the only v2 score whose oracle

instrumented): after the fail ReplayPlayer.PerformFail -> ReplayFailIndicator.Display() ramps the track frequency

to 0 over 1000 ms (osu.Game ReplayFailIndicator.cs TransformBindableTo(trackFreq, 0, audio_sweep_duration)). The

gameplay clock then approaches failTime + 1000 only asymptotically, while PlayerRunner.poll (oracle/PlayerValidation.cs)

waits for FrameStableTime >= maxEnd + 1000. The real Player's fail path therefore needs an oracle change, e.g. also

emit when GameplayState.HasFailed/ScoreProcessor failed and the clock has stalled. That changes oracle.dll and so

the cache fingerprint (it would invalidate data/oracle-cache): orchestrator decision. Classification: harness tooling

(validation-mode exit condition). No result either way.

| variant | runs | match | other |

  • MISMATCH (model ≠ lazer), score before the first judgement. When the schedule stops before any judgement

    • (judgement_count 0, completed false), lazer/oracle report total_score_without_mods = 1000000, but the model

    reports 0. Every other field agrees: total_score 0, accuracy 1, rank X.

  • Lazer source: ScoreProcessor.Reset(storeResults) (osu.Game/Rulesets/Scoring/ScoreProcessor.cs:438-470) first

    • runs updateScore() on the simulated perfect play (so TotalScoreWithoutMods = the maximum, 1,000,000 + max

    bonus). It then resets TotalScore.Value = 0 but not TotalScoreWithoutMods, which keeps the maximum until

    the first real judgement calls updateScore() again.

  • The model starts from totalScoreWithoutMods := 0 (model/OsuModel/Sim/Scoring.lean:70).
  • Minimal repro (NoMod): data/beatmaps/505083.osu data/replays_v2/7742845812.osr --schedule explicit:F, where F

    • holds the single line 0. oracle: 1000000, osu_eval: 0. The fuzz case was 7737946658 (DC) stop.

  • Reachability: only with a schedule that ends before the first judgement. That is never the case for catchup,

    • perframe or dense1ms (they always run to the end), and lazer rejects beatmaps with no objects. In real play it

    corresponds to quitting before the first object.

  • Classification: model bug (spec omits a lazer state quirk), tiny surface. Fix: initialise

    • totalScoreWithoutMods to the stored maximum (TotalScoreWithoutMods after the max simulation) instead of 0. Not

    fixed here (spec change, D20/D30).

  • Input-contract divergence (harness vs model): explicit lists that are not non-decreasing, or empty. The oracle

    • rejects them (oracle/Schedule.cs:55,58: "explicit schedule is empty" and "must be non-decreasing"), but the model

    accepts and simulates them. Eval.lean:31 states non-decreasing in its docstring but never checks it, and osu_eval

    parse_explicit doesn't either; e.g. refs 100, 50 give 169 steps. Found through a fuzzer bug (jitter put entry 2

    below entry 1, now clamped). The corrected list matches (536 judgements).

  • Lazer would *rewind* (FSC backwards, RevertResult) on a decreasing clock, which neither side models; the oracle

    • declares it unsupported.

  • Classification: spec/harness contract gap. The model should reject (stage "sim"/"schedule") instead of giving a

    • result for an input outside the model's domain. Low impact (the CLI user would have to supply such a list).

Net effect: gap 2.1-1 is now covered by 50 real-FSC schedules plus 117 perturbed ones. The results are one model bug

on the zero-judgement edge and one rejection gap. Claim (B) covers every mod family listed in §4 #1 except a real

Player fail.

Runs 2026-10-23, part 3 (05:15-05:45): real-Player fail path (D80c)

Separate build. oracle_fail/ is a copy of oracle/ (AssemblyName oracle_fail, output oracle_fail/bin,

wrapper oracle_fail/oracle_fail.sh). oracle/bin and the cache fingerprint are untouched (oracle.dll md5 f14ef22c…

before and after). The lazer, ruleset and framework dlls are byte-identical to oracle/bin. Changes are in

PlayerValidation.cs and Gameplay.cs only, and the oracle code paths are unchanged unless an env var is set:

  • PlayerRunner.poll: once HealthProcessor.HasFailed/GameplayState.HasFailed holds, the runner emits when the

    • frame-stable clock has not advanced for 120 consecutive host updates (exit: fail_stall), with a cap of 200k updates.

    The output gains exit, fail_seen_fst, final_fst and record_count. ORACLE_FAIL_TRACE=1 traces each update

    after the fail.

  • ORACLE_FAIL_REFS_OUT=F writes the host-frame reference times (GameplayClockContainer.CurrentTime at each step).

    • ORACLE_FAIL_GATE=reference makes run's ReplayPlayer gate read the reference clock instead of frame-stable time.

  • difftest/player_pilot.py: ORACLE_PLAYER=oracle_fail/oracle_fail.sh swaps in this build for the player stage

    • (the run stage keeps the normal oracle). difftest/osr_truncate.py cuts a replay's frames and keeps the header and

    trailer bytes. difftest/fail_gate_check.py runs the reference-schedule check below.

Cause confirmed by instrumentation (7739431096, CL). After PerformFail, the gameplay clock advances by a

geometrically shrinking delta: 33 ms per update, then 1.2 ms at update 100, 3e-4 at update 200, 1e-8 at update 500,

and 0 from about update 700. It converges to failTime + 1000 = 150,308.5553515868, so it never reaches the

maxEnd + 1000 = 173,008 that the runner waited for. That was the 100% CPU hang. (Rate 1 is reported throughout: the

sweep acts on the track frequency.) With the stall exit, a player run takes 4-9 s.

Player = oracle run = model on genuine fails, 8/8 (data/wip/fidrun/failpath). The method is that of parts 1-2:

the player's step list fed as explicit: to oracle run and to osu_eval. Totals: 115,365 steps and 5,970

judgements, step_check ok throughout. Every case matched bitwise (steps, every judgement including those after the

fail, statistics, score, accuracy, rank, failed), and run = model on the full eval_diff:

  • 7739431096 CL: natural fail at 149,302.53 ms, rank F, 241,209. Also with +HD+FL (fail at 149,291.8). These were

    • the two jobs that hung in part 2.

  • Forced, frames truncated (failpath/replays/*t.osr): 7740829451t DT+HD+GR (HP-drain fail), 7742834759t

    • EZ+HD+FL+GR+SD, 7742402030t WD+PF, 7743086189t DP (drain). All rank F, with 5-9 judgements after the fail inside

    the 1 s sweep.

  • Controls: 7738511622 EZ+DT+SD and +PF. Live fails, but the ReplayPlayer gate holds (40/79 rejected triggers), so

    • the player does not fail.

**The real Player reproduces the known fail-gate deviation (§2, "Fail-gate deviation") in 5 of 8 constructed

cases** (data/wip/fidrun/failgate). 7742402030 (WD) + PF was cut just after a non-perfect HitCircle hit at T, so the

last frame is T + 9-17 ms; T ∈ {12184, 16095, 21144, 24411, 25943, 26660, 30751, 32443}. When the FSC sub-steps

through T inside a host frame whose GameplayClockContainer.CurrentTime is already ≥ the last frame, lazer's

ReplayPlayer.CheckModsAllowFailure lets PF fail at T. The oracle and the model gate on the frame-stable time T, so

they reject that trigger and fail later, at the next miss. Results:

  • Player vs oracle run explicit:steps: 5/8 differ. One example is total 150 vs 93: the player freezes before the

    • next miss, which the run still applies (statistics Miss 1 vs 2).

  • Player vs oracle_fail run explicit:refs with ORACLE_FAIL_GATE=reference: 8/8 identical apart from FSC

    • sub-step placement (steps differ). The fail time is exactly T in the 5 differing cases.

  • Gate on frame-stable time: = osu_eval 8/8.

This makes the documented (B) deviation a demonstrated model ≠ lazer difference for ReplayPlayer semantics. Live

semantics are unaffected, and in the natural corpus only 7739431096 fails under the replay gate, where the fail falls

outside such a straddling host frame. A plain gate swap does not suit the kind schedules: under catchup, the

reference-gated oracle opens the gate at the first trigger (fail at 11,179 instead of about 12,551 on c12184),

because the catchup reference is already past the last frame. The fix decision belongs to D72 or the orchestrator.

Observation: in the headless host the real player's step list is not run-to-run deterministic. Three runs of

7739431096 gave three different step lists, and the fail time moved by about 6 ms, presumably from the FSC's 10 ms

wall-clock catch-up budget. Each comparison therefore uses the steps recorded in the same run. oracle run stays

deterministic.

Net effect: the real Player's fail path (PerformFail → FailScore, the fail sweep, judgements during the sweep) now

agrees with the oracle and the model on every genuine fail tested (8 runs, 6 failing), except for the known

reference-vs-frame-stable gate when a trigger lands in a host frame that straddles the last replay frame.

docs/final-audit.md

Final-proof audit (D68), 2026-10-23 ~01:00 UTC

This audit was independent and adversarial. It checked whether the end-to-end theorem eval.evaluate_refines_open

(Eval/JsonFinal.lean), once runWith and RunBudget land, means what the project claims: "the Rust osu_eval

computes exactly the spec OsuModel.Eval.evaluate". Read-only: no proof or spec was edited. The state audited is

HEAD 7f61100 plus the uncommitted WIP in the tree (json's ev_strictOk, simcore2's D67b edits). The audit file

used was proofs/audit.txt from 00:02.

Verdict.

  • The statement is strong: total correctness, every result field compared, accept/reject mismatches excluded.
  • No hypothesis was found that is false on real inputs today. The axioms are standard and no sorry is used.
  • Three MAJOR issues would make the finished claim weaker than advertised:
  • M1: RunBudget as drafted is false for Wiggle (WG) on long maps.
  • M2: the theorem is not instantiated at the binary's environment.
  • M3: the untranslated CLI shell (argument parsing and the JSON printer) is outside the theorem and is not

    • listed as trusted.

  • None of the three is a soundness bug, and none is critical.
  • There are 12 minor items.

Findings: 0 critical, 3 major, 12 minor.

---

1. Statement (ev_topRel, E2EBase.lean)

∃ r, eval.evaluate env bm osr opts sched = ok r ∧ ev_topRel r (OsuModel.Eval.evaluate (abs env) (bytesS bm) (bytesS osr) (ev_optsS opts) (ev_schedS sched))

  • Total correctness. = ok r rules out Aeneas fail (overflow, out-of-bounds index, division by zero,

    • to_bits of NaN) and divergence. So Rust release-mode wrapping arithmetic can never be reached on these inputs.

  • Ok / Ok. The relation is R = ev_resS r R.playable, an equality over all 23 fields of

    • OsuModel.Eval.Result. 22 of them come from the Rust result. Only playable is taken from the spec side,

    because the Rust result does not carry it. The --dump-playable path has its own theorem,

    eval.playable_for_refines.

  • Err / Err. The relation compares E.stage = ev_stageS e.stage, and ev_stageS is injective (7 distinct

    • strings).

  • Mixed cases (Rust Ok and spec error, or the reverse) are False. So "same stage" never hides an

    • accept/reject disagreement. The intermediate relations ev_rjRel and ev_eRel also map mixed cases to False.

  • Weakening 1 (minor m1): the rejection reason text is not compared. osu_eval prints the reason in

    • {"rejected": ...}, so the theorem does not imply byte-identical rejection lines (D33/D34, documented). The

    headline wording ("identical output") should say "identical results; same rejection stage".

  • Weakening 2 (minor m2): float fields are compared as Lean Floats. FunsExternal maps every Rust NaN

    • pattern to the model's single NaN (§4). If a NaN ever reached an output field, the printed hex (hex_d of the

    real bits) could differ from evaltest's. The audit did not look for a reachable NaN output field, and nothing

    proves that none exists.

2. Hypotheses and vacuity

Hypotheses of eval.evaluate_refines_open, plus what simcore2 and json say the final theorem will have:

| Hypothesis | True on real inputs? | Evidence |

|---|---|---|

| O.runWith (js_EvalOpen) | becomes a theorem | Being proved (simcore2). It must disappear from the final statement (see m11). |

| O.lzmaBound = ev_lzmaBound | consistent | lzmaAloneDecode is an opaque @[extern], so the property is uninterpretable in the logic and cannot be refuted. model/c/lzma_shim.c caps the buffer at max_out+1 and errors when len > max_out (lines 32-64), so it is true of the shim. Trusted, listed in §5. |

| InputBounds.h64 | consistent (platform) | System.Platform.numBits is opaque (32 ∨ 64), so the hypothesis is neither provable nor refutable. True on x86-64. |

| InputBounds.bmLen, osrLen | yes | Lengths of real files are < 10 MB. |

| InputBounds.decLines (∃ N ≤ 2^61, dec_pathOk N ∧ lines < 2^31 − 1 ∧ each line < N) | yes | Take N = max line length + 1. For example 2742997.osu has 1150 lines and a longest line of 163 chars. dec_pathOk N needs, for every string shorter than N, < 2^32 control points and calculatePath < 2^62 points. The control points are ≤ the line length. The spec path is bounded by its fuel: bSpline gets 10^8 iterations × degree points per segment, a circular arc ≤ 2^31 (int-saturated), Catmull 100 per point. That is ≤ 10^8·cps + …, which is below 2^62 for any cps < 2^35. |

| PlayableBounds.sliderPaths | yes | Same fuel argument (optimiseCatmull := true). |

| PlayableBounds.decodeTime / .gameplay (GpbBounds: st/cpe/cpt/pp/nest/refl/stk/atb incl. GenOk ∀ψ) | yes | These are all size bounds. Measured on 2742997.osu + 7738504340.osr (WG DF MU): 758 objects, Σ(nested+1) = 1699 (< 2^31), path ≤ 286 points, cumulative length ≤ 143, nested ≤ 8, 5 breaks. GenOk's "every position map ψ" clause is still bounded, because the path fuel bound does not depend on the positions. |

| PlayableBounds.simCtx (ev_mkBoundsS; the WIP adds ev_strictOk, derived) | yes | Frames: 18178 (< 2^32; and ≤ the decompressed text ≤ 2^28 always). Top kinds ∈ {circle, slider, spinner}: true by construction of adaptObject (model/OsuModel/Eval/Adapter.lean:89-100). "∀ ms G, AutoGen.generate P ms = ok G → G.size < 2^62": each generator loop has fuel 10^7 (AutoGen.lean:166/215/233), so G ≤ objects·(3·10^7 + c) < 2^62 for every mod list. |

| hopts (override mods ev_mcOk, length < 2^61) | yes | What parse_mods produces (but see M3). |

| hsched (explicit refs·10^8 + 4 < 2^61) | yes | refs < 2.3·10^10. |

| RunBudget (D67a/c; not committed yet; simcore2 draft, STATE 23:3x) | NO for some real inputs (M1) | See below. |

| Stack (D57, not a hypothesis) | trusted | §5 row. |

The spec values that the hypotheses quantify over are the Rust values for this input. For example

osu_eval and evaltest (the compiled Lean spec, data/wip/end-to-end-eval/bin/evaltest) give byte-identical

output on 7738504340 (md5 8178c46b…), so the measured sizes are the spec's own.

M1 (MAJOR, would be partial vacuity): RunBudget with Wiggle's worst-case constant

  • simcore2's draft (STATE 23:3x):
  • K c n = objects.len·(n+n+4)
  • RunBudget c n B0 := steps.len·K ≤ B0 ∧ B0 + simUnj s0·(n+n+4) + objects.len·(4n+8) + 1 < Usize.max
  • What n is. n is the custom-state cost that discharges simCSH: sim_ar_cs uses

    • n = s3b_csCostFrom vis_mods 0. s3b_vmCost (.Wiggle _) = s3c_W = 2^31 + 2^25 (Sim3/SB_CS.lean:485,

    SC_Wiggle.lean:92). That is the int32 worst case of n1 = preempt/100 and n2 = duration/100. The real value

    is about 10-100 per object.

  • Consequence with WG. 2n+4 ≈ 2^32.05, so RunBudget needs steps·objects (+ judgements) < 2^64/2^32.05 ≈

    • 4.15·10^9. Steps at catchup are about 0.115 per ms of map length; at dense1ms about 1 per ms.

  • The WG replays in the corpus (all 4 have status ok in index_v2) pass. The largest is 7738504340: catchup

    • steps·objs = 2.5·10^7, dense1ms 2.2·10^8.

  • Other real maps fail. Of the 9419 osu! beatmaps in data/beatmaps, 12 have last-object-time(ms)·objects >

    • 4.15·10^9, so WG + dense1ms is outside the theorem for them. 2147769.osu (12000 objects, 55 min) is outside it

    even under catchup: about 3.8·10^5 steps × 12000 ≈ 4.5·10^9.

  • Effect. On those inputs the final theorem is vacuous. It is not wrong.
  • Fix (pick one):
  • (a) Charge Wiggle its real per-call cost: n_i = preempt_i/100 + duration_i/100 (+13 for the other

    • handlers), so the per-step budget is Σ over alive objects of (2·n_i+4).

  • (b) Make the budget per instance. An instance's trackers only grow when its own object is updated, so

    • steps·(2·n_i+4) ≤ B_i per instance, without the objects.len factor.

  • (c) At least use #alive instead of objects.len in K. Alive objects are ≤ ~30.
  • Whichever is chosen, state RunBudget on spec/input values (steps = the spec ctx's steps.size, or a bound

    • from frames/refs), not on the Rust ctx. Make it a named §5 row with the numeric margin.

  • Without WG, n ≤ 13 and RunBudget holds with a margin of about 2^20.

3. Counting honesty

  • The 6 class_overrides entries (became_alive, on_killed, spinner_result, update_bonus_score,

    • update_spinner, part_present):

  • The hypotheses are overflow headroom (completed_spins bounds, to be folded into RunBudget by D67c) or

    • state/ctx well-formedness. That is acceptable as "PROVED".

  • But they also take engine contracts E : s3b_TfEng P, X : simTfX P and U : simTfU P. These are

    • structures whose fields are ∃ o', callee = ok o' ∧ spec …, i.e. callee refinements. proof_status's regex

    (= ok/_refines in the binder text, PROP_COND for def … : Prop) cannot see inside structure types.

  • s3b_tfEng_s2 : s3b_TfEng s2_tfOk exists. No instance simTfX s2_tfOk or simTfU s2_tfOk exists yet

    • (grep). They are easy (s2_tfOkS_UT, update_transforms_refines), but the step loop must provide them.

  • (m4) Classify structure hypotheses that have = ok fields as CONDITIONAL unless an instance at the concrete P

    • is audited.

  • All 23 alias rows (refines_aliases.txt):
  • The 3 proved aliases are real refinements against spec defs: s2_is_skip (an inline == "-12345"),

    • sim_hr_index_spec (HitResult.toNat) and js_mk_ctx_full (OsuModel.Sim.mkCtx, no open callees).

  • The 20 FRAGMENT aliases are only credited as COVERED through the call graph. That is sound, because a

    • FRAGMENT tag alone never counts.

  • COVERED (35 entries): the call-graph rule (all Rust callers proved or covered, reachable from a proved

    • caller) is sound for end-to-end composition. Every covered entry's parent is proved against the real spec.

  • 15 random PROVED entries:
  • Checked: circle_position, apply_decode_defaults, replay_state_diff, check_hittable, binary_search_f64, fmod1,

    • post_process_breaks, rotate_vector, block_vt, add_timing, f64_radians_to_degrees, step_times_of, break_lt,

    barrel_roll_update, add_difficulty.

  • 11 are unconditional refinements against the model def.
  • 4 are not against a spec def:
  • block_vt is against s3b_vtS, a copy of a local let vt. It is bridged in input_block_periods, so it is

    • really COVERED.

  • break_lt is against an inline expression of the spec's local lt. This is acceptable.
  • barrel_roll_update is stated against an explicit Rust-state update, not .barrelRoll of

    • playfieldUpdate.

B. Vacuity of the new hypotheses (task 1)

RunBudgetIn (RunBudgetS on the spec ctx plus D77 e2AccBudS)

  • What changed. RunBudgetS is now (2U + unj + 1)(2n+4) + objs(4n+8) + 1 < 2^64 − 1 ∧ (U+1)·2·10^6 ≤ 2^54.

    • U = runBudgetNeed = the sum, over steps, of the active-list size. So the pass-1 factor steps × objects is

    now Σ alive, which is pass-1 fix (c). The Wiggle cost n is still the worst case 2^31+2^25, but it now

    multiplies U, not steps·objects.

  • Corpus evidence. The runbudget checker uses a cheap bound U ≤ steps·objects: 69353 of 69384 triples

    • ((map, replay) × schedule × {own mods, +WG}) are cleared by it. The worst real case so far, computed exactly

    (rbcheck exact, exact.jsonl), is 2147769.osu + 7738496475.osr under dense1ms:

  • 3,297,117 steps, 12000 objects, U = 14,541,791 (max active 18), unj = 24,334
  • lhs64 = 1.7·10^8 with n = 1 (HD)
  • With WG (n ≈ 2^31.02), the first conjunct needs 2U + unj < ~4.2·10^9, i.e. a margin of about 140×.
  • The second conjunct gives 2.9·10^13 ≤ 1.8·10^16, a margin of about 600×.
  • What a failure would take. Under WG, a map would need U > ~2·10^9 (an average of ~600 alive objects for a

    • 55-minute dense1ms run). Without WG it would need U > 9·10^9. Neither is realistic.

  • Status. M1 is resolved, conditional on the checker's final PASS (2 of the 33 residue triples were done at

    • 04:40). The checker computes U on a VERBATIM copy of the StepInv definitions, compared by

    tools/runbudget/check_defs.py, and a selftest compares the loop against the recursive definition. That is the

    right design.

  • e2AccBudS is Σ(nested+1)·(1 + 2·#AccuracyChallenge) ≤ 2^64 − 1. Real values are ≤ ~25k·3. It could

    • only fail with ~10^14 AC mods (an adversarial --mods list).

SchedFramesIn (every spec step has frameIndex ∈ [−1, frames.size))

  • When it can fail. In simulateSteps (Sim/Schedule.lean:84-131) idx only increases when

    • frameTime(idx+1) ≤ proposed, and frameTime(size) = +∞. So idx reaches frames.size iff a proposed time is

    +∞. idx never goes below −1, because proposed < frameTime(-1) = −∞ is impossible. With no frames, idx stays −1.

  • Kind schedules (catchup/perframe/dense1ms): true on real inputs. The references are r0, the frame times and

    • endT (dense1ms: floor + 1 steps below endT). Frame times are sums of lazer-parse-limited deltas (≤ int.MaxValue

    each, ≤ 2^28 frames), so they are finite. The manual clock moves by ±16.67 ms or a min/max with finite values.

    Gameplay start and endT come from finite object times.

  • Explicit schedules (minor N2): false if a ref is +∞. parse_explicit uses double_parse, which accepts

    • Infinity (Net/Parse.lean:22,148). On such input the Rust indexes frames[size] (Aeneas fail, i.e. a panic

    and exit 101) while the spec rejects. That is a disagreement outside the theorem, but never a wrong score.

  • Cheap fix: reject non-finite explicit refs in both the spec and parse_explicit, or add the condition to the

    • §5 CLI row.

  • Derivable? Only with an IEEE fact ("finite ± 16.67, min/max of finite values stay finite", plus a bound on

    • sums of bounded deltas) about the opaque F64 operations. Lean's core Float arithmetic is opaque to the

    kernel, so this cannot be proved without a float model. Keeping it trusted is justified. The §5 text should

    state the kind-schedule argument above and the explicit +∞ case.

  • m8 (still open, minor): top kinds, the autogen size, frames < 2^32 and now tk are provable by construction

docs/lazer-builds.md

Lazer builds whose gameplay logic matches the pinned 2026.1005.0-lazer

Written 2026-10-21. Pinned build: 2026.1005.0-lazer = ppy/osu 9a10d935b0 (LAZER_COMMIT), osu-framework 2026.921.1.

Sources: the /api/v2/changelog streams lazer and tachyon, git history of ppy/osu and ppy/osu-framework

between neighbouring release tags (blobless partial clones, compared with git log/git diff --stat), and the

client_version that lazer writes into every .osr (LegacyReplaySoloScoreInfo.ClientVersion).

score.build_id is a per-platform build row

The build_id on a score is not the changelog build id. The changelog says 2026.1005.0 = build 8969. Scores

carry 8963/8964/8967/8968 instead, and /changelog/8967?key=id returns 404. Each row is one client binary per

platform. The API doesn't expose the mapping, so difftest/fetch_v2.py learns it: for each new build_id it

downloads up to 2 replays and reads client_version. Observed so far (table builds in data/index_v2.sqlite):

| build_id | client_version | class |

|---|---|---|

| 8816 | 2026.711.0-lazer-windows | X |

| 8845 | 2026.726.0-lazer-windows | X |

| 8871 / 8873 / 8874 | 2026.804.2-lazer-{macos,windows,android} | X |

| 8936 / 8938 | 2026.921.0-lazer-{windows,macos} | A |

| 8963 / 8964 / 8967 / 8968 | 2026.1005.0-lazer-{linux,macos,windows,android} | A (pinned) |

| 8981 / 8983 / 8984 | 2026.1013.0-tachyon-{macos,linux,windows} | B |

All platform builds of one version come from the same git tag. The platform-specific code (desktop vs mobile

hosts and input handlers) only changes how *live* input is sampled. It does not change how a recorded replay is

judged. The recorded frames are the replay.

Class A: gameplay-identical (used as ground truth)

2026.918.0-tachyon, 2026.920.0-lazer, 2026.921.0-lazer, 2026.1005.0-lazer, on any platform.

Lineage: 2026.918.0-tachyon → (+4 commits) 2026.920.0-lazer → (+1) 2026.921.0-lazer → (+1) 2026.1005.0-lazer.

Each tag is an ancestor of the next.

| range | osu changes (full diffstat) | osu-framework |

|---|---|---|

| 918.0-tachyon → 920.0-lazer | ranked-play chat focus fix, "block PMs" setting UI, localisation source, ppy.osu.Game.Resources 2026.909.0→2026.918.0, framework bump. Files: RankedPlayChatDisplay.cs, AlertsAndPrivacySettings.cs, a test, osu.Game.csproj, osu.{Android,iOS}.props | 2026.917.0 → 2026.918.0: only Audio/Track/Waveform.cs (waveform preallocation; editor/visual) |

| 920.0 → 921.0-lazer | framework bump only (osu.Game.csproj, props) | 2026.918.0 → 2026.921.0: only osu.Framework.csproj (SPIRV shader-compiler package downgrade; rendering only) |

| 921.0 → 1005.0-lazer | framework bump only (osu.Game.csproj) | 2026.921.0 → 2026.921.1: image decode type restriction (TextureUpload.cs, AppleTextureLoaderStore.cs) and clipboard (MacOS/SDL3/WindowsClipboard.cs). Security hotfix; no input, clock, transform or gameplay code |

None of these touch osu.Game.Rulesets.Osu/, osu.Game/Rulesets/{Scoring,Judgements,Objects,UI,Replays,Mods}/,

osu.Game/Beatmaps/, osu.Game/Scoring/, osu.Game/Screens/Play/, or any framework input, timing or transform

code. The only resource change (Game.Resources) is samples and textures. Gameplay hit areas don't depend on it:

the argon and triangles skins are code, and a user's skin is unknown anyway (ISSUES G4). 2026.918.0-tachyon has

not been seen in the feed yet.

I did not extend the set further back. 2026.911.0-tachyon → 918.0 touches DrawableRuleset.cs,

RulesetInputManager.cs, PoolableDrawableWithLifetime.cs and an osu-framework jump 2026.901.0→917.0, and would

need a line-by-line audit. 2026.804.2-lazer and older lazer releases are many tachyon cycles behind.

Class B: conditionally equivalent (collected under a 10% quota, analysed separately, never ground truth)

2026.1001.0-tachyon, 2026.1004.0-tachyon, 2026.1005.1-tachyon, 2026.1013.0-tachyon. They branch off

2026.921.0-lazer, so 2026.1005.0-lazer is *not* their ancestor. Changes in judgement-relevant paths since 921.0:

  • ConvertHitObjectParser: object positions are clamped to [0, 512] during parsing (#38844, in 1001.0+). Same

    • result as the pinned build only for maps whose x/y are all in [0, 512].

  • APIMod.ToMod() was replaced by an extension method (#38986, 1013.0), and Mod now implements IConfiguredMod

    • (#38961). These are intended to be behaviour-preserving, but mod-settings deserialisation now goes through new code.

  • ScoreProcessor: parameter renames only. DrawableRuleset: an audio mixer for hitsound volume (#38990; audio only).
  • Drain-time thresholds (#38987) and flashlight difficulty attributes (#38982): difficulty/pp only.
  • osu-framework 2026.930.0 → 2026.1008.0 (SDL3 raw keyboard on Windows, which affects live input only;

    • ThrottledFrameClock/VRR; a RectangleF interpolation typo fix; BASS update). Not audited line by line.

Class X: everything else

Rejected. Their replays are deleted after probing.

Default

If the build is unknown or unmapped, only class A counts. fetch_v2.py decides from the replay's own client_version

(minus the platform suffix), never from the build id alone.

docs/lazer-coverage.md

Lazer / osu-framework code coverage of the oracle corpora (2026-10-22)

Question: which lazer and osu-framework code does the oracle actually execute on our differential-test corpora?

Which judgement- or score-relevant branches does it never take? Is that logic in the Lean model? And do targeted

inputs that do take those branches agree between the model and the oracle?

Headline. The judgement core is 113 files: DHOs, SliderInputManager, spinner tracking, hit policies, hit windows,

score/health/judgement processors, the FSC, the replay input handler, the replay decoder, the gameplay mods, and the

framework's KeyBindingContainer, Interpolation and clocks. On the 2675-job corpus it reaches **80.8% of lines

(4393/5437), 69.7% of branches (1785/2562) and 75.1% of methods**.

The code that makes gameplay decisions is effectively fully covered. Every never-executed line in the core was

classified (§3):

  • Only 5 judgement/score-relevant, reachable gaps were found. All five are modelled in Lean.
  • The rest of the uncovered core code is one of:
  • unreachable in .osr playback: rewinding, spectator frames, pause or seek, non-frame-stable playback, live input

    • devices;

  • unreachable for the osu! ruleset: other rulesets' results and hit windows, invariant throws;
  • not judgement-relevant: UI, samples, settings UI, HUD, skinning.

Targeted generators (difftest/covfuzz.py) now hit all 5 gaps, confirmed by re-measuring coverage. They gave

1200/1200 model-vs-oracle matches (400 jobs × catchup/perframe/dense1ms, 14k judgements), plus 420 earlier

exploratory jobs, also all matching. No mismatch was found, so nothing was added to ISSUES.md.

1. Method

  • Tool: coverlet.console 10.1.0 (IL instrumentation; line and IL-branch coverage), installed with

    • dotnet tool install -g coverlet.console.

  • Driver: difftest/lazer_cov.py (run / merge / report / branches). Each chunk is one

    • tools/heavy coverlet … --target covbin/oracle --targetargs "batch --list …" call, sized to take ≤ 10 min

    (CHUNK rule). Coverage json is merged by summing hits.

  • Instrumented oracle. It is a separate plain (non-R2R) Release build of the unchanged oracle/oracle.csproj:

    • dotnet build -c Release -m:1 -o data/wip/lazer-coverage/covbin.

  • It incrementally reuses the existing lazer obj outputs, so the osu.Game*.dll files are byte-identical to the

    • lazer build outputs, and osu.Framework.dll is the nuget dll.

  • The deployed R2R oracle in oracle/bin/Release/net10.0 and its result cache are never touched or read, except for

    • the read-only sanity check below.

  • coverlet rewrites the dlls in covbin in place for the duration of one call and then restores them. If a call is

    • killed, covbin must be rebuilt: delete the 3 dlls, then rebuild.

  • osu-framework line info. This comes from the nuget symbol package (ppy.osu.framework 2026.921.1 .snupkg

    • → osu.Framework.pdb). Its CI paths (D:\a\osu-framework\osu-framework\…) are mapped to the local

    osu-framework/ checkout at the same tag. Instrumented assemblies: osu.Game, osu.Game.Rulesets.Osu,

    osu.Framework.

  • Sanity: instrumentation does not change results.
  • 391 instrumented job outputs had a deployed-oracle cache entry with the same options, and all 391 are

    • byte-identical (cKKK.check.json, cache_equal).

  • Another 30 stable perframe jobs were re-run on the deployed oracle: 30/30 identical. A further 400/400 covfuzz

    • jobs are identical too.

  • Interpreting the data.
  • Coverlet "branches" are IL conditional-branch arms. ?., ??, is patterns, foreach and switch tables

    • generate many arms that have no source-level meaning, so the triage is driven by **never-executed lines inside

    entered methods (branches --lines) and by never-entered methods**. Branch arms were used only for

    single-line conditions.

  • Known artefact: a break; inside a foreach (it compiles to leave) can be reported as unhit even when the

    • preceding lines ran (LegacyDrainingHealthProcessor.cs:88, :105).

  • Generated code (obj/, source generators) is excluded.

Reproduce:

python3 -I difftest/lazer_cov.py run --list data/wip/lazer-coverage/lists/X.txt --name X --chunk 40 -- --schedule catchup [--replace-mods]
python3 -I difftest/lazer_cov.py merge && python3 -I difftest/lazer_cov.py report --md OUT.md
python3 -I difftest/lazer_cov.py branches --lines --files 'SliderInputManager|HitPolicy'    # triage listing

Driver script: data/wip/lazer-coverage/runall.sh. Raw data: data/wip/lazer-coverage/runs/* (json.gz per chunk,

instrumented outputs, checks), merged_corpus.json.gz (corpus only), merged.json.gz (+covfuzz), and report_*.json.

Corpora measured (2675 jobs, 0 oracle errors)

| run | jobs | schedule | content |

|---|---|---|---|

| syn_cu | 210 | catchup | synthetic synA-D (data/wip/rust-sim; difftest/synth.py: circles/sliders/spinners, edge timing, notelock, frame gaps, stable+lazer format) |

| simmods_cu / _pf / _d | 1310 / 220 / 41 | catchup / perframe / dense1ms | the 37 sim-mods job corpora (data/wip/rust-sim/simmods/w_*, modgen_sim pools M4-M8/ALL with settings; real and synthetic maps), --replace-mods |

| stable_cu (+_b) | 300 | catchup | random sample (seed 7) of the real stable replays (data/replays, auto-Classic) |

| stable_pf | 60 | perframe | another 60 stable replays |

| v2_cu | 474 | catchup | lazer scores (data/replays_v2): every one of the 374 mod combinations at least once, 3 per combination for the 20 most common |

| v2_pf | 60 | perframe | 60 more lazer scores |

| covfuzz (targeted, §4) | 400 | catchup | difftest/covfuzz.py seeds 1 and 2 (seed 2 with random ALL-pool mods) |

2. Coverage tables (corpus, before the targeted inputs)

After adding covfuzz, the judgement core goes to 81.0% of lines (4402/5437) and 70.1% of branches (1795/2562). Every

newly hit line is one of the §3 targets, plus OsuModTargetPractice.cs:215.

The module totals are low because most of osu.Game is UI, online, database, editor and so on. The per-area rows are

the meaningful ones. In several areas the coverage is dominated by visual or settings code, for example "osu ruleset:

UI" (cursor trails, smoke, follow points) and "framework: input" (keyboard, mouse buttons, touch, tablet, joystick,

focus: replay input bypasses these and injects actions through ReplayState).
