Mods

Files: ModSettings.lean (APIMod decoding), Mods.lean (hooks of the simple mods),

ModRandom.lean (Random + repositioning utilities), ModTargetPractice.lean (TP generation,

ModConfig.allHooks). Entry point: Settings.toMod acronym settings : ModConfig, then

load bytes (configs.map ModConfig.allHooks).

Hook points and order

Mod (in Playable.lean) has one optional field per interface that GetPlayableBeatmap consults

(WorkingBeatmap.cs:276-352), applied in this order, each phase in mod-list order:

  • applyAfterConversion (IApplicableAfterBeatmapConversion): ST.
  • applyToDifficulty: EZ, HR, DA, TP (AR ×0.5). Float arithmetic, list order (HR+TP ≠ TP+HR).
  • OsuBeatmapProcessor.PreProcess, ApplyDefaults (with the modded difficulty).
  • applyToHitObject (for each mod, for each object): HR (vertical flip), MR, CL (ClassicSliderBehaviour).
  • PostProcess (stacking, on reflected positions).
  • applyToBeatmap (with the mod index): HD (FirstObject, TimeFadeIn = 0.4·preempt for non-sliders and all

    • nested objects), TC/GR/DF/SI/TR/WG/DP (FirstObject), FR (TimePreempt += StartTime − lastNewComboTime), RD,

    TP (regeneration, then FirstObject), WU/WD (beginRampTime, finalRateTime), AS (precedingEndTimes).

IApplicableToBeatmapConverter / IApplicableToBeatmapProcessor are implemented by no osu! mod. Every other mod

(rate, fail, input, transform-at-runtime, visual) has no beatmap-side effect; NS/SY implement IApplicableToBeatmap

but only capture visual state. Lazer enforces no compatibility here: any list (duplicates included) is applied.

Beatmap-derived mod state is returned in PlayableBeatmap.modStates (ModState: firstObject, timeRamp,

precedingEndTimes), with object references (ObjRef) that carry the beatmap epoch (bumped when TP replaces

the object list, so an earlier FirstObject shows as gone). The simulation needs these.

Details that mattered:

  • PathControlPoint.Position ignores assignments that compare == to the current value, and a new control point

    • starts at (+0,+0): negating a zero coordinate keeps +0 (Mods.setControlPointPos).

  • Reflections/flips/rotations rebuild the path from the modified control points (`new SliderPath(points,

    • ExpectedDistance)), then nested positions follow (updateNestedPositions`); nested times are not regenerated.

  • ST sliders are fresh Sliders: GenerateTicks resets to true, the tail is a StrictTrackingSliderTailCircle

    • (dump: st=1).

  • TP circles get ApplyDefaults at StartTime = 0 (Kiai = EffectPointAt(1)), hence effect points (kiai) are now

    • decoded, and Random's downbeat test needs the time-signature numerator; both are dumped.

  • Random's % beatLength and getAngleDifference's % 2π are exact IEEE fmod (DotNet.fmodF64/fmodF32).

Settings (APIMod.ToMod)

Settings.toMod mirrors APIMod.ToMod for the osu! ruleset: case-insensitive acronym lookup (UnknownMod

otherwise), settings in GetSettingsSourceProperties() order (table checked against bmtest modinfo), each

present key parsed with Bindable<T>.Parse semantics on the Newtonsoft value (JsonVal: long/BigInteger/double/

bool/string/null): Convert.ChangeType rules (Convert.ToInt32(double) half-even with overflow, bool.Parse,

int/double/float.Parse, enum via Enum.Parse(input.ToString()), BindableBool's "1"/"0"), then the setter:

BindableNumber clamp + decimal precision snap + equality no-op (OsuModel.Net.Framework.Bindable, the single

implementation, diff-tested in nettest), DA's DifficultyBindable (extended-range clamp, no snap), nullable seeds;

a failing parse keeps the previous value. WU/WD ValueChanged cross-constraints are run. Defaults come from the

initialisers (e.g. WG strength = 1.00000001490116).

Mod test results (2026-10-21)

run_corpus.py --mods single:SEED:ACR (one mod, randomised settings) / --mods random:SEED (1-5 mods in random

order, duplicates and incompatible combinations allowed, randomised settings incl. strings/bools/nulls/huge ints/

off-grid and out-of-range numbers, unknown keys/acronyms, lowercase acronyms). Every line of the dump is compared,

including the decoded settings (mod lines) and the beatmap-derived mod state (modstate lines).

| corpus | mods | maps | bit-identical |

|---|---|---|---|

| real maps (first 400) | each of the 48 osu! acronyms alone | 48 × 400 | all (after fixing MU's MinValue callback; MU re-run 1000/1000) |

| real maps + test resources | random combos (seeds 11, 14) | 1625 + 1853 | all |

| version-rewritten real maps (v3..v13, v128) | random combos ×2 | 1200 | 1200 |

| fuzz.py (seed 5) + gen.py (seed 9) | random combos (seed 13) | 3000 | 2998, 2 skipped (resource limit, below) |

| RD alone, TP alone (real maps) | | 150 + 150 (+400 each in singles) | all |

| TP alone on fuzzed maps (incl. the 3 that exposed the sample-lookup exceptions) | | 203 | 199 (8 of them both fail with ArgumentOutOfRangeException), 4 skipped (resource limit) |

Bugs found by the test and fixed: PathControlPoint equality no-op (−0), case-insensitive acronyms,

MuteComboCount.MinValue follows InverseMuting, TP's sample lookups throwing ArgumentOutOfRangeException

on fuzzed maps (NodeSamples index / getClosestHitObject(-1)), and (before using the Net layer) decimal snapping.

Residuals / not covered:

  • Resource limit. Maps on which lazer itself exceeds a 640 MB GC heap (OutOfMemoryException, e.g. fuzzed maps

    • with enormous tick/beat counts; TP on maps with huge end times) are skipped, and the model is not run on them

    (it would need similar memory). Two fuzzed maps hit this even without mods.

  • Random/TP without a seed are non-reproducible in lazer (RNG.Next()); the model rejects them.
  • BCL conversions in settings decoding (Convert.ToInt32, bool.Parse, ToString for enums, Newtonsoft number

    • classification) are tested, not transcribed from source. JSON numbers like 1e400 (Newtonsoft overflow) and

    duplicate JSON keys were not generated.

  • Acronym lookup is ASCII case-insensitive; OrdinalIgnoreCase on non-ASCII letters (e.g. ı) is not modelled.

Trust assumptions / environment

  • Numerics. These are the OsuModel.Net assumptions: glibc 2.39 libm for

    • Math.Atan2/Cos/Sin/Acos, which only the perfect-curve arc uses, and F64.sqrt/F32.sqrt

    being correctly rounded.

  • Rulesets. All four rulesets are available, as in the game. This affects Mode: lines.

    • bmtest registers a RulesetStore with ids 0–3 for the same reason. Maps whose final mode is

    not 0 are reported (mode N) and not converted.

  • Culture. Like oracle/, bmtest runs with InvariantGlobalization=true. The only

    • culture-sensitive call on this path is the "osu file format v" header test

    (StartsWith(..., InvariantCulture), Decoder.cs:75). The model uses ordinal comparison,

    which agrees except on files that put ICU-ignorable characters (e.g. a second U+FEFF) before

    the header.

  • Not modelled: JSON beatmaps. Files starting with { (JsonBeatmapDecoder) give an error.
  • Not modelled: UTF-32 BOMs and unpaired UTF-16 surrogates. These also give an error.
  • Not modelled: GetPlayableBeatmap's 10 s timeout. bmtest uses CancellationToken.None.
  • Fuel bounds. The model replaces three potentially unbounded loops with a fixed iteration

    • cap ("fuel"). Each cap is far beyond anything lazer can finish within its own 10 s timeout:

  • Bezier subdivision: 10⁸ steps.
  • Slider tick loop: 10⁷ ticks per span.
  • The others are structurally bounded.
  • Pathological pooled-buffer read: harmless. convertPathString reads beyond the point list

    • (stale ArrayPool memory) only when a later segment is empty. That segment always throws, so

    the line is dropped anyway (argued in the code).

  • Irrelevant state is not modelled. Samples, colours, metadata, storyboards, kiai and effect

    • points have no gameplay effect. Their only influence on the modelled state is whether parsing

    them throws, which drops the whole line. That is modelled wherever such a parse shares a line

    with modelled data: sample banks of hit objects, and the sample/effect fields of timing

    points.

Differential test

  • model/bmtest/ (C#). Has a ProjectReference to lazer's osu.Game.Rulesets.Osu. Build:

    • dotnet build -c Release -m:1 -p:BuildProjectReferences=false (lazer's Release build already

    exists).

  • It loads a file exactly like the game: Decoder.GetDecoder<Beatmap>(LineBufferedReader),

    • then .Decode, then FlatWorkingBeatmap.GetPlayableBeatmap(osu, mods).

  • It dumps every gameplay-relevant field as raw bits:
  • beatmap level: version, difficulty, stack leniency, timing and difficulty points, breaks;
  • per object: kind, start/end time, position, stack height/offset, stacked position, scale,

    • radius, preempt, fade-in, combo fields, hit windows, MaximumJudgementOffset;

  • per slider: repeats, velocity, tick distance, multipliers, distances, expected distance,

    • durations, end positions, all control points with types, every calculated path point and

    every cumulative length (via reflection);

  • per spinner: duration, spins required, bonus spins;
  • per nested object: everything above plus path progress, span index and start, repeat

    • index, spinner duration.

  • bmdump (Lean, model/BmDump/Main.lean). Prints the same format from the model.
  • model/bmtest/run_corpus.py. Runs both over a corpus and compares line by line. For error

    • lines only the stage (decode or playable) is compared.

  • model/bmtest/fuzz.py. Generates mutated maps aimed at decoder and geometry edge cases:
  • number formats and extreme values;
  • missing and extra fields;
  • path types and degrees, duplicate points, colinear and degenerate perfect curves;
  • section headers, comments, line swaps and duplicates;
  • format versions;
  • CR/CRLF line endings, BOMs, UTF-16 and invalid UTF-8;
  • hold, spinner and odd type bits.
  • bmtest sorttest N SEED | bmdump sorttest. Checks the introsort model against .NET's

    • List<T>.Sort on arrays with many ties.

Test results (2026-10-21, NoMod)

(Since the mods work, the dump also has effect lines, the time-signature numerator on timing lines, kiai= on

every object, classic= on sliders/heads/tails and st= on tails; NoMod re-checked on 300 maps.)

| corpus | maps | bit-identical |

|---|---|---|

| crawled data/beatmaps (1500, all v14/v128) + lazer test resources (80 .osu + 45 from .osz/.olz; 33 non-osu modes compared as mode N) | 1625 | 1625 |

| real maps with rewritten format version (v3..v13, v128: +24 ms offset, old stacking, v<8 tick multiplier, int coordinates, legacy perfect/catmull rules) | 1500 | 1500 |

| fuzz.py mutations (seeds 1, 2) | 6000 | 6000 (incl. 72 where both sides fail decode/playable at the same stage, 335 non-osu modes) |

| gen.py synthetic (seeds 7, 8) | 7000 | 7000 |

| introsort vs List<T>.Sort (sorttest 3000 1) | 3000 arrays | 3000 |

Residual mismatches: none observed. The test is sensitive: disabling the single "no extension when last two path

points are equal" quirk produced mismatches in 300 synthetic maps. Gaps: real old-format (v<14) maps only via

test resources and header rewriting (the crawler only returned v14); mods not yet tested (hooks only);

ICU culture header comparison (see trust assumptions); decoder error *messages* are not compared, only the stage.

Reproduce:

cd model && lake build bmdump && (cd bmtest && dotnet build -c Release -m:1 -p:BuildProjectReferences=false)
python3 -I bmtest/run_corpus.py --work /tmp/bm            # default corpus
python3 -I bmtest/fuzz.py OUT 2000 1 @seeds.txt; python3 -I bmtest/run_corpus.py --work /tmp/fz OUT/*.osu
python3 -I bmtest/gen.py OUT 3000 7;   python3 -I bmtest/reversion.py OUT 3 @list.txt
# mods (wrap in tools/heavy; run_corpus caps the .NET heap and kills any process above ~1 GB RSS)
../tools/heavy python3 -I bmtest/run_corpus.py --work W --mods random:11            # combos
../tools/heavy python3 -I bmtest/run_corpus.py --work W --limit 400 --mods single:1:TP
dotnet bmtest/bin/Release/net10.0/bmtest.dll modinfo                              # settings table
docs/model-eval.md

End-to-end model: OsuModel.Eval (.osu + .osr → result)

OsuModel.Eval.evaluate : Env → ByteArray → ByteArray → Options → Schedule → Except Rejection Result

(model/OsuModel/Eval.lean) composes the beatmap model, the .osr decoder, the adapter and the simulation:

beatmap bytes ── LegacyBeatmapDecoder.decode ──────────────────────────────┐  (OsuModel.Beatmap)
.osr bytes ───── Osr.decode: container, LZMA (trusted), lazer score JSON ──┤  (OsuModel.Replay.Osr)
                 decode-time GetPlayableBeatmap(bitfield mods) — can only throw   (LegacyScoreDecoder.cs:94)
                 resolveMods (oracle --mods / --replace-mods / --no-classic; Autoplay check)
                 getPlayableBeatmap(gameplay mods) ─ toSimPlayable ─────────┤  (OsuModel.Eval.Adapter)
                 Replay.decode frame text (v<5 offset) ────────────────────┤  (OsuModel.Replay.Frames)
                 Config.ofMods, steps(schedule), Sim.run ──────────────────┘  (OsuModel.Sim)
  • Env — the fixed environment (D10) as data: OsuModel.Eval.defaultEnv (Eval/Env.lean, the bits of

    • difftest/env-1024x768.json).

  • Options — the oracle's mod options (oracle/Program.cs ResolveMods): modsOverride (--mods, APIMods decoded

    • with APIMod.ToMod; each replaces a decoded mod with the same acronym or is appended; unknown acronym → reject),

    replaceMods, noClassic. Then Player's DeepClone (identity on the decoded settings).

  • Schedule — kind catchup|perframe|dense1ms or explicit refs (D9; equivalence is claimed per schedule).
  • Result — oracle schema fields: decoded / effective mods, is_legacy_score, true gameplay rate, schedule

    • (r0, end, gameplay start, last frame time, reference and step counts), per fail semantics (live / ReplayPlayer,

    the latter none = "same_as_live" exactly when the oracle prints that) the score/health state, maximum

    statistics, and the processor-order judgement list.

  • Rejection — stage + reason for every input on which lazer throws (see "Rejections").

Executable: `evaltest BEATMAP.osu REPLAY.osr [--schedule S|explicit:FILE] [--mods JSON] [--replace-mods]

[--no-classic] [--no-judgements] [--steps] [--timing] [--dump-playable PATH] (model/EvalTest/Main.lean`); prints the

oracle's JSON schema with doubles as raw IEEE bits ("0x…") and mods as acronym lists + decoded settings.

.osr decoding (model/OsuModel/Replay/Osr.lean)

| lazer (osu.Game/…, 2026.1005.0) | Lean |

|---|---|

| IO/Legacy/SerializationReader.cs:28-63 ReadString (0 byte = null), ReadByteArray (<0 null), ReadDateTime (negative ticks → IOException; > MaxValue → ArgumentOutOfRange); BCL BinaryReader (Read7BitEncodedInt ≤5 bytes, ReadBytes short at EOF, EndOfStream) | readString, readByteArray, readDateTime, read7BitEncodedInt, readBytes, readLE |

| Scoring/Legacy/LegacyScoreDecoder.cs:47-118 field order; GetRuleset (oracle: only id 0) | readContainer |

| :56 IsLegacyScore = version < FIRST_LAZER_VERSION (30000000) (LegacyScoreEncoder.cs:74) | DecodedScore.isLegacyScore |

| :88 OsuRuleset.ConvertFromLegacyMods (osu.Game.Rulesets.Osu/OsuRuleset.cs:96-148) | convertFromLegacyMods (NC⊃DT, PF⊃SD, CN⊃AT; default settings) |

| :91-92 auto ModClassic for stable | decode (bitfieldMods) |

| :94 decode-time GetPlayableBeatmap(bitfield mods) | Eval.evaluate (only its failure is observable; skipped when identical to the gameplay playable's mods; unseeded RD/TP dropped) |

| :98 beatmapOffset = BeatmapVersion < 5 ? 24 : 0 | Replay.decode t beatmapVersion |

| :107-118 online id width by version, score info for version ≥ 30000001 | readContainer |

| :120-121, :168-193 readCompressedData (≥5 property bytes, 8 size bytes, LzmaStream), StreamReader.ReadToEnd | readCompressedText (LZMA via lzmaAloneDecode, then Beatmap.streamReaderDecode; fast path for BOM-less valid UTF-8) |

| :123-146 JsonConvert.DeserializeObject<LegacyReplaySoloScoreInfo>; Mods = readScore.Mods.Select(m => m.ToMod(ruleset)) | decodeScoreInfo, apiModToMod (Settings.toMod = APIMod.ToMod), checkScoreInfo |

| :268-352 frames | OsuModel.Replay.decode (Replay/Frames.lean, sim agent) |

What in the lazer score JSON matters for evaluation: only mods (acronyms + settings): it replaces the bitfield

mods entirely (absent key → empty list; a stable-style bitfield in a lazer replay is ignored then). statistics,

maximum_statistics, rank, online_id, user_id, client_version, total_score_without_mods, pauses only populate

the decoded ScoreInfo, which playback never reads (the ScoreProcessor recomputes everything; maxima come from the

simulated autoplay). They are type-checked only because a Newtonsoft failure aborts the import. IsLegacyScore

(version) matters: Classic auto-add, and Relax's Update is a no-op for non-legacy scores (OsuModRelax.cs:75-76).

Trust boundary: LZMA

c/lzma_shim.c (osu_lzma_alone_decode, ~60 lines) calls the system liblzma (xz-utils 5.4.5, liblzma-dev,

statically linked into evaltest only; lakefile.lean target lzma_shim.o). Lazer uses SharpCompress' managed

LzmaStream on the same .lzma "alone" format. Assumed equal on well-formed streams (every corpus replay decodes

to identical frames — checked implicitly: the judgement lists match). On corrupt/truncated streams lazer may return

partial data or throw differently; the model rejects ("lzma: data error"/"truncated input"). Output is bounded

(256 MiB).

Adapter (model/OsuModel/Eval/Adapter.lean)

toSimPlayable : Beatmap.PlayableBeatmap → Sim.Playable: field-by-field the C# getters the oracle's

--dump-playable reads (oracle/Dump.cs:68-215); CreateJudgement() max/min results from the kind, Classic slider

behaviour and the strict-tracking tail (judgementOf, with source lines). playableJson writes the adapter output in

the oracle's dump format (keys the sim reads; fade_in, judgement, repeat_count, tick_distance*,

generate_ticks, end_position are not part of the sim interface).

Rejections (ISSUES G12)

The model rejects (stage, reason) exactly where it can determine that lazer throws, and in the documented

non-modelled cases:

| stage | cause | lazer |

|---|---|---|

| beatmap-decode | decoder errors (Beatmap model), non-osu! ruleset map | throws / converts (not modelled) |

| replay-decode | EOF in header, bad 7-bit length, negative/huge date ticks, ruleset ≠ 0 | same exception types |

| replay-decode | LZMA failure, < 13 payload bytes | IOException / SharpCompress (trusted boundary) |

| replay-decode | lazer score JSON: invalid JSON, trailing content, mods/settings/statistics null, wrong types | Newtonsoft / NullReference |

| replay-decode (decode-time playable) | GetPlayableBeatmap throws with the bitfield mods | throws |

| mods | unknown override acronym; Autoplay/Cinema | oracle ArgumentException |

| playable | GetPlayableBeatmap throws (e.g. TP sample lookups), unseeded RD/TP (G5) | throws / non-reproducible |

| replay-frames | Parsing.ParseFloat/ParseInt failures | FormatException / OverflowException |

Not modelled (lazer fails, model gives a result or fails differently): OutOfMemoryException / the 10 s

GetPlayableBeatmap timeout on pathological maps (resource limits of the environment, docs/model-beatmap.md

"Residuals"); exceptions in PopulateMaximumStatistics (difficulty calculation for legacy scores) and

StandardisedScoreMigrationTools; Newtonsoft's lenient JSON extensions (comments, trailing commas, single quotes,

numeric strings) — the model's JSON reader is strict.

Test (difftest/eval_diff.py)

run feeds the same (beatmap, replay, options) to oracle batch (cached) and evaltest, compares input/schedule

fields, both fail semantics' final state and every judgement (i, n, type, result, RawTime bits, combo, health bits,

failed; ReplayPlayer: identity fields only — the sim records per-judgement combo/health for live only) and localises the

first difference (beatmap / replay-decode / sim). playable compares evaltest --dump-playable with

oracle --dump-playable on every emitted key, bit-exact. jobs --corpus stable|v2 [--gen-mods POOL] builds job lists

(random mod overrides from modgen_sim.py).

Results (2026-10-21, lazer 2026.1005.0, evaltest built 14:47 with the sim at e2f362d)

Agreement = every compared field identical (judgement lists bit-exact incl. RawTime/health bits, statistics, score,

accuracy bits, rank, fail state of both semantics, schedule fields, decoded/effective mod acronyms).

| corpus | mods | schedule | jobs matching | judgements |

|---|---|---|---|---|

| stable replays (data/replays, Classic auto) | own (bitfield) | catchup | 300/300 (earlier sim build: 600/600, 512k) | 216,565 |

| stable replays | own | perframe | 300/300 | 216,565 |

| stable replays | own | dense1ms | 10/10 | 4,342 |

| stable replays | own + --mods [NF] | catchup | 100/100 | 62,682 |

| stable replays | own, --no-classic | catchup | 100/100 | 62,682 |

| stable replays | random M5 pool (rate/fail/DA/HR/MR/…, random settings), --replace-mods | catchup | 150/150 | 169,554 |

| stable replays | random M6 pool (RX/AP/AL/SG/SO/ST + rate/fail) | catchup | 150/150 (2/150 with the sim before e2f362d: RX+WU / RX+AS+ST tails, sim-side) | 169,543 |

| stable replays | random M7 pool (transform/position mods; sim M7 in progress) | catchup | 99/100 with the sim sources of 16:05 (90/100 with the 14:47 build; all mismatches contain TR; remaining one: NF+HR+AD+TR, sim-side) | 99,776 |

| lazer replays (data/replays_v2, JSON mods with settings) | own | catchup | 450/450 | 484,658 |

| lazer replays | own | perframe | 300/300 | 319,271 |

| lazer replays | random M5, --replace-mods | catchup | 100/100 | 103,856 |

| synthetic edge-case .osr (truncation, ruleset 1, negative date, corrupt LZMA, lazer JSON variants, bad overrides) | | catchup | 12/14 agree (8 both reject, 4 match); 2 documented divergences: Newtonsoft trailing comma (lazer accepts), unseeded RD (G5) | |

Adapter losslessness (eval_diff.py playable, oracle --dump-playable vs evaltest --dump-playable, every key

the sim reads, bit-exact): stable own mods 100/100, lazer own mods 100/100, random beatmap-side mods (HR, EZ, DA, MR,

ST, CL, HD, TC, GR, DF, WG, FR, SI, TR, DP, WU, WD, AS, DT, HT + seeded RD/TP) 100/100 (+60/60 again after fade_in

joined the sim interface), random M5 100/100, the 2 M6 and 10 M7 mismatch jobs 12/12. Hence every mismatch above is

sim-side (beatmap model and replay decoding are exonerated: the playable is bit-identical and decoded mods/frames

feed identical schedules: steps, last_frame_time agree). Same-binary check: evaltest --sim-playable <oracle dump>

gives exactly the adapter-path result on all 10 M7 mismatch jobs. Found on the way (sim-side, STATE "Requests"):

Sim.magnetUpdate index-out-of-bounds panics on MG/RP jobs (results still matched on the tested jobs).

The sim sources are compiled into evaltest as they are on disk (the sim agent edits them concurrently). All rows

were re-run with the 16:05 build (sim e2f362d + on-disk WIP): 2059/2060 jobs, 1,909,494 judgements bit-exact; the

only mismatch is the M7 TR job above.

Performance (evaltest wall time per replay, whole pipeline incl. process start and JSON output, measured on the

shared 2-core VM at load 2–8): median 0.5–1.2 s, ~62 MB RSS; beatmap decode + playable + .osr decode + adapter (+

dump) ≈ 0.15 s median, the rest is the simulation; dense1ms ≈ 6 s. The oracle needs ~1.5–6 s per replay on the same

machine (catchup). Eval-side code follows the Lean perf rules (no float literals or Nat.toFloat in loops; byte-level

readers on ByteArray; UTF-8 fast path via String.fromUTF8?; arrays used linearly).

Re-run on the final sim (HEAD 791e4a1 / 883e873 sim sources, 2026-10-21 evening; evaltest built in a HEAD worktree)

PANIC output on stderr fails a job; ReplayPlayer judgements are compared with combo/health/failed (JRec.*RP).

BarrelRoll environment bug (eval-side, fixed in 95499c3). All BR mismatches of the first pass (5/15 per-mod BR jobs,

the stable-ALL WU+BR job and perframe 7738055654 NF+TR+DF+BR+BM) had one cause: Eval.defaultEnv (Eval/Env.lean)

lacked the HitObjectContainer ancestor chains (hoc_chain_first/hoc_chain of difftest/env-1024x768.json; the

Env fields default to #[]), so Sim.curHoc recomposed an *empty* chain (identity) instead of the rotated playfield

chain. Because the replay-to-screen conversion and the hit/follow tests used the same wrong matrix, the geometry was

merely re-expressed in different float coordinates: results changed only through rounding (slider tails/ticks at the

follow-area boundary), which is why 10/15 BR jobs still matched. Localisation: simtest (same sim sources) on the

oracle's --dump-playable with the env file matched the oracle exactly where evaltest did not; a debugging trace

(per-step HOC and slider DrawInfo, screen-space mouse) of the NF+BR job 1661649/4857687379 was bit-identical to the

oracle's ORACLE_DHO_STATES env dump on all 38,065 steps (HOC), 10,100 slider samples and 31,935 mouse samples (the

oracle probes at step start = model state after the previous step). Env.lean now carries both chains and a #guard

that they recompose the dumped HOC DrawInfos bit-exactly. The sim (incl. the brScale "placeholder") is confirmed.

ReplayPlayer semantics fully compared (oracle printed a separate replay_player) on several hundred of these jobs; no PANIC.

docs/model-sim.md

Gameplay simulation model (model/OsuModel/Sim, model/OsuModel/Replay)

The Lean model of what lazer's drawable/judgement layer and processors do with a playable beatmap, decoded

replay frames, mods and a step schedule (docs/model-architecture.md: Sim.run env pb rep mods steps).

All arithmetic uses OsuModel.Net (bit-exact .NET float32/float64, same op order as the C#).

Files

| file | content |

|---|---|

| Sim/Basic.lean | Vec2, Mat3 (osuTK), MatrixExtensions ops, DrawInfo.ApplyTransform, Vector2Extensions.Transform, HitResult + extension predicates, Precision.AlmostEquals, C# % 1 |

| Sim/Playable.lean | Playable (the sim's input interface; every field the drawable layer reads) + loader for the oracle's --dump-playable JSON (raw bits) |

| Replay/Frames.lean | frame text → OsuReplayFrames (LegacyScoreDecoder.readLegacyReplay, stable fixups, backwards-frame filter, FromLegacy) |

| Sim/Schedule.lean | FSC stepping (applyFrameStability + SetFrameFromTime), reference schedules catchup/perframe/dense1ms; mirrors oracle/Schedule.cs |

| Sim/Geometry.lean | Env (HitObjectContainer DrawInfo, argon path radius, HOC size), DrawInfo chains for HitReceptor / slider head / DrawableSlider / spinner AspectContainer, CompositeDrawable.Contains (rounded corners), SliderPath PositionAt/CurvePositionAt, follow-area test |

| Sim/State.lean | per-object and global state, Config (mods), Ctx |

| Sim/Step.lean | the frame-stable step (§3.1): processors → input → lifetimes → DHO updates; judgement application + result chain; hit policies; circles, slider heads/ticks/repeats/tails, sliders, spinners |

| Sim/Scoring.lean | ScoreProcessor (combo, statistics, accuracy, standardised score, rank, maxima by simulated autoplay), OsuHealthProcessor / OsuLegacyHealthProcessor (drain-rate searches, per-step drain, break periods, combo-end bonus, fail), score multiplier (NF, CL) |

| SimTest/Main.lean | simtest executable: (playable dump, frame text, env, mods, schedule) → oracle-like JSON (times/health/accuracy as hex bits) |

Harness: difftest/sim_diff.py (oracle batch + simtest + judgement-by-judgement compare), difftest/osr.py

(.osr read/write; LZMA = trusted boundary), difftest/synth.py (synthetic maps/replays), difftest/real_jobs.py

(crawled corpus), difftest/env-1024x768.json (environment data from oracle --dump-env).

Oracle additions (oracle/Dump.cs): --dump-playable PATH, --dump-env PATH (batch: directories, <job index>.json);

default outputs are byte-identical to before (checked on the 5-replay corpus).

Step semantics (one frame-stable step at time t, Sim.stepOnce)

  • Processors (FrameStableComponents): JudgementProcessor.Update (HasCompleted), DrainingHealthProcessor.Update

    • (drain DrainRate * (clamp(t) - clamp(t - Elapsed)) unless in a no-drain period; Elapsed = t - t_prev, 0 in step 0).

  • Input (InputManager.Update): replay position (float lerp of the two frames around the handler time) →

    • HitObjectContainer.ToScreenSpace (step 0 uses the pre-layout HOC matrix, see Env) → if the position changed:

    MouseMove (sliders' screenSpaceMousePosition, spinners' tracker position in AspectContainer space) and hover

    update; then ReplayState.Apply: releases, then presses (KeyBindingContainer Unique mode: an action already

    held is not re-propagated); presses go to HitReceptors in input-queue order (earliest start first, ties smaller

    ChildID first); a receptor handles the press iff CanBeHit() and IsHovered (even if the policy rejects the hit);

    high-frequency MouseMove to sliders; hover update if not yet done this step.

  • Playfield mods: none in scope.
  • Lifetimes (LifetimeEntryManager.Update): future→alive in (LifetimeStart, ChildId) order (DHO apply: Idle state,

    • receptor/slider/spinner state reset, Idle lifetime from hit-state transforms), then deaths in activeEntries order

    (OnKilled → UpdateResult(false)), alive dictionary with .NET Dictionary free-list reuse (AliveObjects tie order).

  • DHO updates in HitObjectContainer child order (later start first; ties larger ChildID first). Slider subtree:

    • SliderInputManager.Update (tracking) → ticks → repeats → tail → head (lifetime check, auto-miss, PostProcessHeadJudgement)

    → slider result. Spinner: Tracking → rotation tracker (atan2f, ±180 normalisation, SpinnerSpinHistory) →

    CheckForResult (end: miss remaining ticks, result by progress) → bonus ticks.

applyResult = DrawableHitObject.ApplyResult: result + RawTime, lifetime from the hit-state transforms

(LatestTransformEndTime formula incl. the +1), then the result chain: hit policy HandleHit (StartTimeOrdered

forced misses recurse and reach the processors before the causing hit) → HealthProcessor → ScoreProcessor.

Both fail semantics (live Player / ReplayPlayer gate t >= lastFrameTime) are run side by side.

Mods (M5, M6) — Sim/Mods.lean (Config.ofMods), Sim/AutoGen.lean, hooks in Sim/Step.lean/Sim/Scoring.lean

Mod list order is significant everywhere (lazer applies any combination, in list order; the oracle's --replace-mods

gives exactly the list). Config.ofMods walks the list once and builds:

  • Rate (Config.trueRate): GetTrueGameplayRate = 1 * AggregateFrequency * AggregateTempo; each IApplicableToTrack

    • mod adds its bindables in list order and AggregateBindable folds 1 * 1 * v1 * v2 …. HT/DT add SpeedChange to

    Frequency (adjust_pitch) or Tempo; NC/DC add freqAdjust = Default (1.5 / 0.75) then tempoAdjust = s / Default

    (so NC 1.51 ≠ DT 1.51 in the last bit for some s); WU/WD/AS add a time-varying SpeedChange. Used by

    SpinnerRotationTracker.AddRotation ((float)(delta * |rate|)) and SpunOut.

  • Time-varying rate (IUpdatableByPlayfield, phase P3 = Playfield.Update, before lifetimes/DHOs, list order):

    • TimeRamp SpeedChange = BindableDouble{Precision 0.01}.Value = ApplyToRate(t) (Math.Round(ramp, 2)), initial value

    ApplyToRate(+∞) (FinalRate.TriggerChange in ApplyToTrack); AdaptiveSpeed `SpeedChange = clamp(DampContinuously(…,

    targetRate, 50, Elapsed)) plus its OnNewResult` handler (runs first in the result chain — mod handlers are

    subscribed when the pooled DHO is created, before the HitObjectContainer's — on circles/heads with a preceding end time;

    recentRates window of 8, consistency, Lerp).

  • Fail (Step.triggerFailure): TriggerFailure → (ReplayPlayer gate) → All(PerformFail) over

    • IApplicableFailOverrides in list order, short-circuit: NF/CN veto, EZ spends a life and refills Health := MaxValue

    (the bound bindable), ModFailCondition allows. Fail conditions: SD (+ fail_on_slider_tail), PF (relevance rule),

    TP (SD-like). AC: fired from ScoreProcessor.updateScore on a *change* of Accuracy (Standard, set first) /

    MaximumAccuracy below MinimumAccuracy — after the result was counted; the recorded health is the value after both

    processors (EZ refill by an AC trigger is visible on that judgement).

  • Rank: ScoreProcessor.rank is only recomputed on Accuracy.ValueChanged (an exact change), then

    • AdjustRank of every IApplicableToScoreProcessor (HD/FL: X→XH, S→SH); initial rank = adjusted X.

  • Score multiplier: OsuScoreMultiplierCalculatorV2 with ScoreMultiplierCalculator.CalculateFor (combinations in

    • registration order, then singles of the remaining types in list order; float settings subtract in float

    (size_multiplier - 1, start_scale - 2); DA uses the unmodded BeatmapInfo.Difficulty). Also checked against the

    oracle's total_score = round(total_score_without_mods * multiplier) on every job.

  • Classic: classic_note_lock → LegacyHitPolicy(400 - (AP ? 200 : 0)) + head CanBeHit = !slider.AllJudged;

    • classic_health → legacy health processor; no_slider_head_accuracy is beatmap-side; tail sample / early fade visual.

  • Relax (legacy replays only; --lazer-replay makes it a no-op): P3, alive objects by start time, break at

    • t < start - 12, hover flags of this step's P2, IsMouseInFollowArea(DrawableSlider.Tracking) — the bindable copied in

    the previous step's DrawableSlider.Update (model: OState.drawableTracking), presses/releases via the

    KeyBindingContainer (do not touch the replay-state diff).

  • Autopilot: OsuAutoGenerator (literal, including List<OsuAction> aliasing: { Actions = lastFrame.Actions } shares

    • the list and later Clear(); Add(a) mutates every frame sharing it), at most one frame per step injected as

    MousePositionAbsoluteInput in P3 (immediate MouseMove + hover); the next P2 re-applies the replay position.

  • Alternate/SingleTap: interceptors are the last children of the KeyBindingInputManager, so they see every press

    • first (last-added first); a blocked action stays in PressedActions; PeriodTracker state shared by P2 and P3.

  • SpunOut: spinner HandleUserInput = false (no MouseMove to the tracker, no Tracking assignment), OnUpdate:

    • Tracking = IsSpinnableTime, `deg = RadiansToDegrees((float)(Elapsed / Clock.Rate) * (float)(1.01*spins/duration) *

    π * 2); Clock.Rate` is the FSC rate set at step start (before this step's P3), the rotation uses the live rate.

  • StrictTracking runtime: DrawableSlider.Tracking true→false (in DrawableSlider.Update, before children) misses the

    • strict-tracking tail unless the slider is judged or t < StartTime. Found: a slider can then be judged before its

    head, so judged sliders must keep updating their subtree (the head still auto-misses).

  • TD, SV2: markers (multiplier 1). AT/CN: rejected by the oracle (they replace the replay) — out of scope.

M7: drawables, transforms, pools — Sim/Transforms.lean, Inst/pools in Sim/State.lean, updateState/customState/subtree updates in Sim/Step.lean

  • Transform engine (Sim/Transforms.lean): literal Transformable + TargetGroupingTransformTracker with

    • RemoveCompletedTransforms = false (DHOs): per-member trackers (Position, Scale, Rotation, Alpha), (StartTime, ID)

    order, AddTransform drops later same-member transforms and applies immediately when Start < now || End <= now

    (forced rewind if Start <= now), the rewind branch, ReadIntoStartValue on first application, property setters keep

    the old value when equal, TransformSequence (Then, Delay, Append re-rounds now + (currentTime - now)),

    LatestTransformEndTime (+1), clearExistingStateTransforms (rewind to double.MinValue, then clear).

  • DHO state updates: UpdateState = clear → UpdateInitialTransforms at Start - Preempt (FadeInFromZero, slider

    • body FadeInFromZero(TimeFadeIn)) → hit-state transforms at Result.TimeAbsolute ?? EndTime → Expire (lifetime end

    now computed by the engine, not a closed form) → ApplyCustomUpdateState handlers: own list, then for a nested head

    the parent's list via the forwarder (two passes). Called from Apply only for re-used (loaded) instances, from

    LoadComplete on the first UpdateSubTree of a *fresh* instance (LoadState.Ready at Apply), and on every judgement.

  • Pools (OsuPlayfield.cs:141-164, DrawablePool.cs): LIFO stacks of instances (circle 20/100, slider 20/100,

    • head 20/100, spinner 2/20 prewarmed/max). Per-instance state survives re-use: members after the free-time clear, bound

    PositionBindable/StackHeightBindable/ScaleBindable copies (their ValueChanged fires only on change, e.g.

    Position = StackedPosition is not re-applied for an identical position), LoadComplete done, and for sliders Size,

    OriginPosition, Tracking, the body's last Refresh and its pending scheduled refresh.

  • Presence (Drawable.IsPresent, DHO override || (Idle && now >= LifetimeStart)): a non-present DHO gets

    • UpdateTransforms but no Update/children/UpdateAfterChildren (Drawable.cs:469-498, CompositeDrawable.cs:907-950):

    a judged slider stops updating its (possibly unjudged, StrictTracking) head once faded. Input is not affected:

    DrawableHitObject.PropagatePositionalInputSubTree/PropagateNonPositionalInputSubTree => HandleUserInput

    (DrawableHitObject.cs:74-78) override the framework's IsPresent && rule, so a faded (alpha 0) judged head stays

    hovered and keeps consuming presses (Classic) until its lifetime ends — also under HD. (docs/mods/transform-mods.md

    §1.7/§8.1 claim the opposite; found by a Relax mismatch and confirmed with the oracle's DHO dump: the dead-alpha head

    was still hovered.)

  • G1 (pooled slider geometry): on apply the body refresh is scheduled (pathVersion change → Scheduler.AddOnce), an

    • immediate refresh happens only if ScaleBindable changed (PathRadius setter). The scheduler runs only while the body

    (SkinnableDrawable, alpha from FadeInFromZero(TimeFadeIn)) is present, i.e. not in a step at exactly the fade start.

    DrawableSlider.UpdateAfterChildren copies the body's Size/PathOffset every step. Observed with the oracle's

    ORACLE_DHO_STATES dump: a re-used instance alive at exactly Start - Preempt keeps the previous slider's

    Size/OriginPosition for one step.

  • Mods (customState): GR/DF (ScaleTo(start).Then().ScaleTo(1, preempt, OutSine)), SI (rotation 360→0 and scale

    • (2,0)→1 InOutSine on circles *and heads*, slider scale 0→1), TP (scale 0.5 → 1 linear), TR (MoveToOffset + MoveTo,

    global theta), WG (System.Random((int)StartTime) 100 ms segments from the position read at handler time — the head's

    second pass reads the moved position), HD (DHO alpha fades for circles/heads/spinners, slider body), Classic early fade;

    first-object rule (IncreaseFirstObjectVisibility, HD/TC skip spinners). P3: DP (Position/Scale from time), MG/RP

    (damped Position towards/away from the cursor ActiveCursor.DrawPosition, slider ball offset after the head result).

stale first step of a re-used instance).

Regression after the M7 core (pools, engine lifetimes, G1, presence gating): all M5/M6 corpora above still 100%

(incl. 100 real M5).

Findings: (1) DHO input ignores presence (above); (3) DrawableHitObject.State lives on the pooled instance: a

re-used spinner tick that was never loaded keeps Miss, so its next miss is a no-op UpdateState (no handlers → no

Transform theta advance); (2) fresh pool instances are in LoadState.Ready (not IsLoaded)

at Apply, so their first UpdateState happens in LoadComplete only — reused instances get it in Apply (one pass

for nested heads, before the parent forwarder exists); this decides Transform's theta sequence.

Totality (G17, 2026-10-21)

The simulation is total and has no silent defaults: no xs[i]!, get!, back!, set!, insertIdx!, getD default

or exOr fallback is left in Sim/*, Replay/{Frames,Osr}, Eval.lean or SimTest/Main.lean. Each access is either

proved in bounds (xs[i]'h, for h : i in [0:n], Vector for transforms, structural bsearchBy, the size

invariant ScoreSt.stat on statistics) or goes through a rejecting accessor (getA/setA/need in SimM).

  • SimM = ReaderT Ctx (StateT St (Except String)). mkCtx, initState, runWith, simulate, steps,

    • references, simulateSteps, mkHealthCfg, computeDrainRate, periodIsInAny, HealthSt.drain,

    AutoGen.generate, Config.trueRate, positionAt, curvePositionAt, sliderGeom, bodyRefresh and reportDelta

    return Except String. simtest prints {"error": …} and Eval rejects with stage "sim".

  • Error classes: internal: … (an invariant violation, which should be unreachable), malformed … (the playable

    • breaks an interface invariant, e.g. a slider without a head or tail), and lazer would throw: … (lazer itself throws

    here, so there is no lazer result):

  • an empty slider path (Path.Vertices[0], SnakingSliderBody.cs:119);
  • Math.Clamp with inverted runtime bounds (drain bounds, frame-time interpolation);
  • Math.Sign(NaN) (ComputeDrainRate, SpinnerSpinHistory);
  • new Period(start, end) with start >= end, or Objects.First(…) with no match (InputBlockingMod.cs:52,55,

    • PeriodTracker.cs:80).

Math.Clamp calls with literal bounds use clampK, whose throwing branch is dead.

  • No partial defs remain (D27, 2026-10-22: the mods-JSON reader Sim/ModsJson.lean is structural / nesting-fuel recursion,

    • Settings.assign uses explicit fuel assignFuel).

  • Gotcha found during the refactor: a nested (← e) inside a && … is hoisted before the whole statement, so it is

    • evaluated even when a is false (classicHead evaluated sliderData for circles). The old code returned default

    there; the total code rejected the input, which exposed it. Use if a then … else pure false.

  • Performance (2026-10-22): the first version of the refactor was up to 3x slower (evaltest 3.5 s -> 10.3 s on

    • 5556876.osu + 7737962141.osr, 25k steps). There were two causes. (1) modifyObj/modifyInst read the state

    with let s ← st and wrote it back with set { s with objs := ← setA s.objs … }. s.objs is then shared with the

    monad state, so every update copied the whole array (O(objects) per update). They now do checkIdx (the range check

    of getA, same message) and then modify fun s => { s with objs := s.objs.modify i f }, which updates in place.

    (2) Without inlining, each getA/ctx/st returned an allocated Except.ok (x, s), and getA also allocated an

    Option, on every access in the per-step loops over all objects (updateHover). The small accessors are now

    @[inline], and getA uses if h : i < a.size. Meaning and signatures are unchanged. Pattern to avoid in hot

    paths: let s ← st; … set { s with xs := (update of s.xs) } for large arrays. Use a check, then modify.

  • Regression after the refactor: model-only re-runs (sim_diff --reuse-oracle) of all 35 M5-M8 corpora (catchup,

    • perframe, dense1ms; synthetic and real) gave 1451/1451 jobs and 259,098 judgements, with 0 PANICs and 0 rejections.

    eval_diff run on 40 stable replays gave 40/40.

Assumptions / scope

  • Environment = the oracle's (D10): 1024x768, default config, argon skin, snaking on. Env data (HOC DrawInfo before/after

    • the first layout pass, HOC size, argon path radius 0x425cb08d) in difftest/env-1024x768.json.

  • Mods in scope: all osu! mods (M5-M8 below); AT/CN replace the replay and are rejected. Mods come as the APIMod JSON list (simtest --mods-json),

    • decoded with OsuModel.Beatmap.Settings.toMod (= APIMod.ToMod, shared with the beatmap model).

  • Beatmap-side mod effects (EZ/HR/DA/MR/RD/TP/FR/ST conversion/CL slider behaviour/HD fade-in/…) are in the playable

    • (oracle dump or OsuModel/Beatmap); the sim implements only drawable/processor-side effects.

  • Not modelled because unobservable here: visual transforms other than those that define lifetimes, samples,

    • rewinding, spectator statistics frames, ClosestPressPosition/hit-event positions, storyboard start time.

  • Frames: decompressed LZMA text is the input; header fields used: beatmap version (offset) from the playable.
  • Fuel-bounded loops (while … fuel) stand in for C# while loops; fuel is far above any reachable count, and

    • running out of fuel is a rejection (Except error), never a silent truncation (G17).

  • NaN payload handling per docs/net-float.md.

Notable lazer quirks found (relevant for any re-implementation)

  • DifficultyRange associates as mid + (max - mid) * ((d - 5) / 5) (docs/lazer-map.md §1.3 wrote * (d-5)/5):

    • 1-ulp health differences otherwise.

  • Hover is recomputed before presses only if the cursor moved in that step; otherwise presses see the hover state

    • of the previous step (a just-alive object under a static cursor can't be hit in its first input step).

  • Input-time state is the previous step's: objects become alive in the lifetime phase after input.
  • Classic heads keep consuming presses (CanBeHit = !slider.AllJudged) only while the head DHO is alive:

    • hit → RawTime + 800 + 1, miss → + 100 + 1 (hit-state transforms + LatestTransformEndTime's +1).

  • An unjudged slider/spinner's Idle lifetime ends at EndTime + 241, circles EndTime + 801.
  • HitAction is set on any hovered press of the head, even a notelocked one, and before PostProcessHeadJudgement

    • runs the head's own updateTracking sees HitAction == null.

  • Within a step, nested judgements come out ticks → repeats → tail → head → slider, and objects later-start-first.
  • AliveObjects ties use .NET Dictionary enumeration order (free-list reuse); modelled.
  • HOC matrix in step 0 is the pre-layout one (scale 1) — only affects the step-0 cursor.
  • Spinner rotation tracker only updates its cursor on actual movement; float.RadiansToDegrees(x) = (x*180f)/MathF.PI.

every slider DrawInfo, OriginPosition, DrawSize and head-receptor matrix sampled while the slider is active is

Known gap found by this check: at the *first* step after a pooled DrawableSlider becomes alive, its

Size/OriginPosition (hence slider and head-receptor matrices) can still be those of the previous slider that used the

drawable: PlaySliderBody.Refresh is scheduled (Scheduler.AddOnce) and the body's scheduler only runs once the body

SkinnableDrawable is present (alpha > 0 after FadeInFromZero). The model uses the final geometry from the start.

Algebraically the head position is unchanged (origin/size*size - origin), so only float rounding of hover/follow

tests in that first step (≥ preempt before the head time, where no hit is possible; only HitAction on a hovered

press could be affected) differs. 133 of ≈105k probe records, all first-records.

docs/net-float.md

.NET numeric primitives in the Lean model (model/OsuModel/Net/)

This file covers the bit-exact model of the CoreCLR (.NET 10.0.13, linux-x64) numeric primitives

that lazer's osu! judgement and scoring code uses.

  • Package: model/ (Lean 4.35.0, package OsuModel, no Mathlib).
  • Library entry point: import OsuModel.Net.
  • Differential tester: model/nettest/ (C# generator) streams into lake exe nettest (Lean checker).

Ground rules

  • F64 := Float, F32 := Float32 (abbrevs). Lean 4.35 defines these as Float.Model/Float32.Model

    • (IEEE bit patterns with one canonical NaN).

  • The operations + - * /, comparisons, neg, ofBits/toBits and ofScientific are

    • kernel-reducible.

  • Compiled, they are the C operators, i.e. the same SSE2 instructions RyuJIT emits. RyuJIT never

    • contracts to FMA and has no x87 excess precision.

  • Everything this library adds is plain Nat/Int code with structural recursion only

    • (OsuModel/Net/Fmt.lean: decode, roundBin = correct RNE rounding, isqrt). It reduces under

    decide +kernel; see OsuModel/Net/Checks.lean (~70 kernel-checked facts, two of them ∀ lemmas).

  • Exceptions are modelled as Except NetExn α. NetExn is one of: format, overflow, argument,

    • argumentOutOfRange, arithmetic.

  • Beware of dot notation. (x : Float).toInt32 resolves to *Lean core's* Float.toInt32, not

    • F64.toInt32. Always write F64.foo x unless x is syntactically typed F64.

NaN

Neither the Lean model nor the Lean runtime can represent NaN payloads or signs:

  • the model has a single NaN, 0x7FF8000000000000;
  • the compiled Float.ofBits/toBits canonicalise NaN (verified).

.NET produces 0xFFF8000000000000 (double.NaN, 0/0) and propagates payloads. The tester

therefore treats any NaN as equal to any NaN, and counts payload differences separately

("nan-payload-diff", informational).

Rule for the model: never branch on the sign or bits of a NaN. Lazer only uses IsNaN, and the

.NET primitives below never look at NaN bits.

The one observable consequence is signalling NaN inputs. They cannot be created by arithmetic

or parsing, only by bit reinterpretation. Math.Pow(sNaN, 0) is NaN on .NET but pow(qNaN, 0) = 1.

The tester reports these cases as "snan-input-diff"; they are not failures and are irrelevant to

lazer.

Primitives

The Status column uses three values:

  • K: kernel-computable definition.
  • E: extern, trusted (glibc).
  • K\*: Lean core definition that is kernel-reducible.

Test op numbers refer to NetTest/Main.lean.

| .NET | semantics / source | Lean | Status | test op |

|---|---|---|---|---|

| a+b a-b a*b a/b (double, float) | IEEE RNE, SSE2 addsd… | + - * / on F64/F32 | K\* | 1–4, 6–9 (+ model 151–159) |

| < <= == > >= != | IEEE (NaN false, +0 == -0) | <, ≤, ==; a > b ↔ b < a, != ↔ !(a == b) | K\* | 5, 10 (+ model 155, 160) |

| unary - | sign flip | -x | K\* | 37, 47 |

| (float)double | cvtsd2ss, RNE, overflow → ∞ | F64.toF32 (convertBits) | K | 11 |

| (double)float | exact | F32.toF64 | K | 12 |

Parsing details (Number.Parsing.Common.cs, Number.Parsing.cs)

The grammar is NumberStyles.Float | AllowThousands:

ws* [+|-] body ws* \0*      (ws = U+0009–000D, U+0020)

Rules:

  • Thousands separator. , is allowed in the integer part *after the first digit*:
  • "1,,0" = 10
  • "1," = 1
  • ",1" and "1.5," are invalid.
  • At least one digit. "1." and ".5" are valid; "." and ".e5" are not.
  • Exponent. e must be followed by [+-]digit, otherwise the parse fails.
  • When the exponent reaches ≥ 10^8 during digit accumulation it saturates to ±int.MaxValue: the

    • result is ∞ or 0 whenever the mantissa is non-zero (e.g. "0.0001e100000000" → ∞).

  • Otherwise the result is the correctly rounded exact decimal, including:
  • overflow → ±∞ (never an OverflowException);
  • "-0" → -0.0;
  • tails of more than 768 digits (handled with a sticky bit).
  • Trailing NULs are accepted only after a number ("1 \0" is valid, "1\0 " and

    • "Infinity\0" are invalid).

  • Infinity/NaN fallback. Trim() with the *Unicode* whitespace set (so " NaN　" is

    • NaN), then an ASCII case-insensitive match against Infinity, -Infinity, NaN, +Infinity,

    +NaN and -NaN. ∞ is not accepted.

Lean's own Float.ofScientific/Float32.ofScientific are correctly rounded and kernel-reducible.

The tester checks them against .NET (ops 200 and 201). Our parser uses its own Parse.decToBits

(through roundBin) so that the rounding code is shared and float32 rounding is direct.

Transcendentals: trusted base

  • CoreCLR calls libm directly. src/coreclr/classlibnative/float/floatdouble.cpp is just

    • return sin(x); (and so on). libcoreclr.so imports sin@GLIBC_2.2.5, pow@GLIBC_2.2.5,

    powf@GLIBC_2.27, … from libm.so.6 (nm -D).

  • JIT. RyuJIT does not inline these on x64. It only constant-folds constant arguments, which

    • also goes through libm via libclrjit.so.

  • Single-instruction intrinsics on x64:
  • Math.Sqrt → sqrtsd
  • Floor/Ceiling/Truncate/Round → roundsd
  • Abs → andps
  • FusedMultiplyAdd → vfmadd
  • Max/Min → vectorised compare/blend sequences with the managed semantics

All of these are modelled exactly (kernel-computable), not trusted.

  • Verified on this VM. nettest jit <x> with `DOTNET_TieredCompilation=0

    • DOTNET_JitDisasm="JitW:*"` shows:

  • Math.Floor → vroundsd …, 9
  • Math.Round → vroundsd …, 4
  • Math.Sqrt → vsqrtsd; MathF.Sqrt → vsqrtss
  • Math.Max → vrangesd + 2×vfixupimmsd (AVX-512; on other CPUs the managed code runs, with

    • the same semantics up to NaN payload)

  • (int)x → vcmpordsd/vcvttsd2si + cmov saturation
  • Math.Sin/Math.Pow/MathF.Atan2 → call (FCall into libm)

With LD_PRELOAD of a shim defining sin, pow and atan2f, .NET returns the shim's values,

which proves dynamic resolution through libm.

  • Lean side. The compiled Lean binary dynamically links the system libm.so.6, with the same

    • symbol versions (sin@GLIBC_2.2.5, …), so both call the identical code.

  • Pinned glibc: Ubuntu GLIBC 2.39-0ubuntu8.x (x86-64). glibc ≥ 2.41 swaps several binary32

    • functions for CORE-MATH versions, and any other libm can differ in the last ulp. Re-run the tester

    after any OS upgrade.

Differential test

cd model && lake build
cd nettest && dotnet build -c Release -m:1
dotnet bin/Release/net10.0/nettest.dll gen <countPerOp> <seed> [op,op,..] | ../.lake/build/bin/nettest
dotnet bin/Release/net10.0/nettest.dll lazer <countPerSetting> <seed> | ../.lake/build/bin/nettest   # needs lazer + oracle builds

Generator inputs. Uniform random bits, plus targeted distributions:

  • specials and their ±2-ulp neighbours (±0, ±∞, quiet and signalling NaN, subnormal/normal

    • boundaries, 2^52 and 2^23 boundaries, int32/int64 limits);

  • moderate exponents and integers, halves and quarters;
  • values with few low bits set (halfway cases);
  • near-float doubles ((float)x ties) and correlated operand pairs (b = ±a ± k ulp);
  • for transcendentals, "human" ranges.

Parsing inputs.

  • exact decimal expansions of binary64/binary32 midpoints (±1 in the last digit, truncated, or with

    • a non-zero tail);

  • R/G17/E16-formatted random values;
  • long digit strings (up to 900 digits, exponents up to ±1200);
  • random strings over a hostile alphabet (,, ., e, signs, whitespace, \0, NBSP, ∞,

    • letters of Infinity/NaN);

  • mutated numbers and symbol case/whitespace variants;
  • a fixed list of edge cases (the probe results above).

Found while testing (now modelled): decimal.CreateTruncating(NaN) is 0.0m with scale 1; BindableNumber clamps

with double.Clamp (IEEE min/max: -0 → +0 at a 0 bound) rather than Math.Clamp; Bindable.Value keeps the old

value when the new one is Equals (so -0.0 never replaces +0.0); osuTK RadiansToDegrees(float) uses

57.29578f (0x42652EE0).

Known gaps / not modelled

  • NaN payload/sign, and signalling NaNs (see above).
  • decimal addition/subtraction/comparison/%, Round with other modes or digits, and decimal parsing

    • (not used by lazer's mod settings path).

  • Random.NextInt64, NextBytes, Shuffle, GetItems; derived-class Random (CompatDerivedImpl); unseeded Xoshiro.
  • osu-framework Interpolation.ValueAt for colours/rectangles/other types; MatrixExtensions.FastInvert.
  • Math.FusedMultiplyAdd, Math.ScaleB, Math.Log2, BitIncrement and other unused APIs.
  • int.Parse / double.Parse with non-invariant cultures, or NumberStyles other than the

    • defaults.

  • Scale int32 overflow inside .NET's number buffer (needs strings of more than 2^31 digits).
  • Lean Float.sqrt itself is kernel-opaque (it uses Nat.sqrt, which is well-founded). Use

    • F64.sqrt instead. It is tested equal to Float.Model.sqrt and to .NET.

docs/proof-pipeline.md

Proof pipeline under the disk limit (research 2026-10-21)

This doc asks which machine-checked route from the Lean spec to a fast evaluator fits this VM. The VM has a

25 GB disk, and 6.0 GB was free when this was written (other agents keep using more). It has 2 cores and

3.8 GB RAM. This doc refines D6 and D8.

All numbers below were measured on this VM unless they are marked *est.* The measurements came from GitHub

release assets, rust-lang dist manifests, archives streamed through wc -c/tar tv (nothing kept on disk), a

blobless sparse clone of mathlib4 v4.35.0 (since deleted), and two small Lean/Rust benchmarks.

TL;DR ranking

| Rank | Route | Extra disk | Rust↔spec link | Verdict |

|---|---|---|---|---|

| 1 | Fast evaluator written in Lean, proved equal to the clear spec in core Lean (no Mathlib), compiled to C. Rust is only a thin FFI/CLI shell. | ~0 GB (the toolchain is already installed) | The *executed code* is the proved Lean code. The Rust shell holds no logic. | Do this now. |

| 2 | Charon + Aeneas + Aeneas Lean lib, with a filtered Mathlib cache (only the ~1.1k modules Aeneas imports) | ~2.3-2.9 GB *est.* | A real Rust→Lean proof. | Feasible later if a pure-Rust core is required. Prove aeneas(rust) = lean_fast. |

| 3 | Charon + Aeneas with our own Mathlib-free Aeneas.Std prelude (upstream definitions copied, proofs re-done) | ~0.75 GB | Real, but the TCB adds our prelude copy and we lose the step/scalar_tac automation. | Fallback if rank 2 doesn't fit. |

| 4 | Verus plus a Lean→Verus spec fn printer | ~1.5 GB *est.* | The printer is unverified, and there is a semantic gap between Lean and Verus (Nat/int, uninterpreted floats). Verus has open float soundness bugs (#3073, #3136, #3194, #3172). | Not recommended. |

| 5 | Our own Rust-subset→Lean translator ("translation validation") | ~0 GB | The translator is unverified, in the TCB, and must model Rust semantics itself. | Weakest. Only as a last resort. |

| ✗ | Aeneas + full Mathlib (lake exe cache get) | ≥7.5 GB | Real | Does not fit. |

1. Exact cost of Charon + Aeneas today

Binaries (prebuilt, no OCaml/opam/nix needed)

  • Aeneas release nightly-2026.10.21-fc321a2, asset aeneas-linux-x86_64.tar.gz: 161 MB download,

    • 595 MB unpacked. Contents:

  • aeneas (42.5 MB)
  • charon + charon-driver (17.7 + 26.2 MB). This is the charon build that matches charon-pin (de8736f7).
  • backends/lean sources plus a prebuilt .lake/build of the Aeneas Lean lib (436 MB). Of that, 171 MB is

    • setup.json, 114 MB is .olean.private, 53 MB is .c and 46 MB is .olean.

  • The nested lean-build-aeneas-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz (69 MB). It can be deleted after unpacking.
  • Binaries only (rank 3) come to ~90 MB.
  • The standalone Charon releases (charon-linux-x86_64.tar.gz, 11.6 MB) are newer than the pin: nightly-2026.10.20

    • is 15 commits ahead of de8736f7. Use the charon that ships inside the Aeneas tarball.

  • No Docker image was found. There is a Nix flake (nix run github:AeneasVerif/aeneas), but Nix would cost more disk.

Rust nightly needed by Charon

  • charon-driver dynamically links librustc_driver-415cc549468a4aa5.so. That file is in the rustc

    • component of nightly-2026-09-17 (verified: the hash matches). rustc-dev is NOT needed at runtime. It is

    only needed to build charon from source.

  • Unpacked sizes:

| Component | Unpacked size |

|---|---|

| rustc | 425 MB |

| rust-std | 168 MB |

| cargo | 37 MB |

| rust-src | 78 MB |

| rustc-dev | 688 MB |

| llvm-tools | ~150 MB *est.* |

  • The minimal profile is ~630 MB. Do not let rustup auto-install the toolchain from charon's

    • rust-toolchain file, because that adds rustc-dev, llvm-tools, rust-src, miri and 8 targets (>1.6 GB).

Aeneas Lean library → Mathlib

  • backends/lean/lakefile.lean contains require mathlib @ "v4.35.0" (rev 56a00585), and

    • lean-toolchain is v4.35.0, which matches our toolchain.

  • 270 files and 49k lines in total. 31 distinct Mathlib imports, mostly Data.BitVec, Tactic.Linarith,

    • Ring, Data.Nat.Log, ZMod, Order.FixedPoints and Tactic.Tauto. The Mathlib users are concentrated in

    Std/Scalar/*, Std/Range, Tactic/{Step,Solver,ScalarTac,Simp} and Data/Range.

  • Transitive closure: 1081 of the 8624 Mathlib modules (12.5% of 98.9 MB of source). Upstream packages:

    • only Batteries, Aesop and Qq. ProofWidgets, Plausible, LeanSearchClient and importGraph get cloned but are not

    imported.

  • Olean size. Mathlib v4.35 publishes .olean, .olean.server, .olean.private, .ilean and .trace.

    • The ratio of build output to source, measured on this toolchain's Init and Std (also module-system code), is

    41-44x. Applied to Mathlib:

  • **Full Mathlib: ~4.5-6 GB *est.*** Add ~1-2 GB for the .ltar copies in ~/.cache/mathlib and ~0.7 GB for

    • Lake's full git clone of mathlib4 (the repo is 506 MB plus the worktree). **That is ≥7.5 GB peak, which

    does not fit.**

  • **Filtered closure: ~0.55-0.8 GB *est.*** for Mathlib, plus ~0.2-0.4 GB for Batteries, Aesop and Qq.
  • Filtering is supported. lake exe cache get Mathlib.Data.BitVec Mathlib.Tactic.Linarith ... (module names,

    • globs or paths) fetches only those modules and their transitive imports. cache get- downloads without

    unpacking, so you can measure (du -sh ~/.cache/mathlib) before you commit the disk.

  • Pruning after download is not safe. Lake treats .ilean and .olean.private as build outputs, and

    • deleting them makes lake build try to rebuild Mathlib modules. Filter *before* the download instead, and run

    lake exe cache clean! afterwards to drop the .ltar copies.

  • RAM: importing ~1.1k Mathlib modules plus Aeneas uses ~1-1.5 GB *est.* (mmapped oleans), which is fine with

    • -j1.

Rank-2 install steps (≈2.3-2.9 GB; run only when no other heavy job is running)

# a) binaries (161 MB download -> keep ~90 MB of binaries + the 436 MB prebuilt lib)
mkdir -p ~/tools/aeneas && cd ~/tools/aeneas
curl -LO https://github.com/AeneasVerif/aeneas/releases/download/nightly-2026.10.21-fc321a2/aeneas-linux-x86_64.tar.gz
tar xzf aeneas-linux-x86_64.tar.gz && rm aeneas-linux-x86_64.tar.gz \
  && rm backends/lean/.lake/lean-build-aeneas-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz
# b) nightly, minimal (~630 MB)
rustup toolchain install nightly-2026-09-17 --profile minimal
#   run charon with: RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN=nightly-2026-09-17 LD_LIBRARY_PATH=$(rustc +nightly-2026-09-17 --print sysroot)/lib \
#     ~/tools/aeneas/charon cargo --preset=aeneas   (rust-src (+78 MB) only if charon asks for it)
# c) proofs/ lake project: require aeneas from local path ~/tools/aeneas/backends/lean.
#    Avoid Lake's full mathlib clone: pre-create shallow clones at the manifest revs
git clone --depth 1 --branch v4.35.0 https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4 proofs/.lake/packages/mathlib
#    (same for batteries/aesop/Qq/... at the revs in backends/lean/lake-manifest.json; verify `git rev-parse HEAD`)
cd proofs && lake exe cache get- Mathlib.Data.BitVec Mathlib.Tactic.Linarith ...   # the 31 seeds; check du
lake exe cache get <same args> && lake exe cache clean!
LEAN_NUM_THREADS=1 lake build -j1

The 31 seed modules are listed by

grep -rhoE '^(public |meta )*import (all )?Mathlib\S*' backends/lean --include=*.lean | sort -u.

2. Mathlib-free alternatives with a machine-checked link

  • Rank 3, own Aeneas.Std prelude. Aeneas output only needs the *names* `Aeneas.Std.{Result, UScalar,

    • IScalar, Vec, Slice, Array, ...}. The definitions are built on core BitVec`, and only the lemmas and tactics

    need Mathlib.

  • A prelude that copies the upstream *definitions* verbatim (about 3-5k of the 14.9k lines in Aeneas/Std) and

    • re-proves only the lemmas we use with core omega/grind/bv_decide keeps the generated code's meaning

    identical to upstream.

  • Trust: Charon, Aeneas, plus a line-by-line diff of our prelude against upstream (script it).
  • Cost: binaries (~90 MB) plus the nightly (~630 MB).
  • Downside: we lose step*/scalar_tac, so the proofs are more manual.
  • Rank 4, Verus with generated specs. A Lean meta-program would print model defs as Verus spec fns.
  • The printer is unverified, and Lean Nat/Int/Float semantics must be mapped by hand.
  • Floats are uninterpreted in Verus, and there are open soundness bugs in its float handling.
  • In effect you get two sources of truth that are kept equal by a tool and by testing. Weaker than ranks 1-3.
  • Disk: 487 MB zip plus a pinned stable toolchain, ~1.5 GB *est.*
  • Rank 5, our own Rust-subset→Lean translator (syn-based, for a restricted style we control).
  • Cheap on disk, but the translator is an unverified TCB component that must get Rust's overflow, cast and

    • float semantics right.

  • The only mitigation is differential testing of the generated Lean against the Rust binary, which makes this

    • no stronger than testing the Rust impl directly against the compiled Lean model.

3. Rank 1: the fast evaluator in Lean (the recommendation)

Shape.

  • model/ already has the clear spec.
  • Add OsuModel/Fast/*: the same algorithm with arrays, indices, in-place updates and incremental state.
  • Prove Fast.eval b r s = Spec.eval b r s with core tactics only (simp, omega, grind, Array.getElem_set

    • lemmas, loop invariants via termination_by recursion). Mathlib is not needed: floats are never reasoned about

    numerically, they only need to be shared syntactically (see verification-tools.md), and the rest is

    Nat/Int/Array/List bookkeeping.

  • Ban implemented_by and @[extern] in our code, because they break the link. The existing Net float layer's

    • externs (libm) are the declared trusted base.

Rust shell.

  • Build the Lean lib as a static lib (lean_lib facet static).
  • Link libOsuModel.a, libInit.a (26 MB) and libStd.a (30 MB) only if they are imported. Also link

    • libleanrt.a, libleancpp.a, libgmp, libuv, libc++ and libunwind from $(lean --print-prefix)/lib.

    Never link libLean.a (312 MB). Keep Lean imports out of the evaluator modules.

  • build.rs links them. At startup, call lean_initialize_runtime_module(), then

    • initialize_OsuModel(1, lean_io_mk_world()), then lean_io_mark_end_initialization().

  • Call an @[export osu_eval] def evalBytes : ByteArray → ByteArray → ... → ByteArray (do .osu/.osr parsing in

    • Lean too, so the shell contains no logic).

  • Alternatively, skip Rust and ship the lake exe directly.

Trust base. The Lean kernel, the Lean compiler (LCNF → C), the runtime, clang, Float externs = Float.Model

(TestFloat-validated) and pinned glibc libm. This TCB is smaller than Aeneas's (no Charon, Aeneas or rustc

semantics) and gives a single source of truth.

Performance (measured on this VM under load 5). The kernel is 100 × 100k in-place updates of `a[i] = a[i]*k1 +

a[i-1]*k2 + c`:

| Variant | Time |

|---|---|

| Rust -O | 25-37 ms |

| Lean, termination_by recursion with FloatArray.set | 52-108 ms |

| Lean, for/Id.run loop | 50-78 ms |

| Lean, naive version | 2.2-3.3 s |

So Lean is ~1.5-3x slower than Rust when written carefully. In-place updates work: the arrays are unique,

there is no copying, and an Array Obj struct-update loop also ran in place (6M object checks in ~30 ms).

The naive version is ~100x slower because of a Lean ≥4.33 pitfall: Float literals compile to a *runtime*

Float.ofScientific call (~55 ns each, since it is now model-implemented), and Nat.toFloat takes ~74 ns.

UInt64.toFloat takes 2.4 ns. Coding rules for Fast:

  • Hoist float constants into top-level defs. Closed terms are initialised once.
  • Use UInt64.toFloat/Float.ofBits, never Nat.toFloat/literals inside loops.
  • Prefer USize/Fin-indexed access with proofs over a[i]!.
  • Keep arrays linear (never alias).
  • Use @[specialize] on higher-order helpers.
  • Grep the generated .c for ofScientific/Nat_toFloat inside hot functions as a CI check.

An osu! replay is ~10^4-10^5 frames × a few objects, so the expected cost is well under 10 ms per replay.

Parsing will dominate.

Plan.

  • Write the spec (in progress).
  • Write Fast and prove Fast = Spec milestone by milestone (the ratchet).
  • Add the Rust FFI shell plus difftest.
  • *Optional, later:* if a native-Rust core is wanted, write it in the Aeneas subset and prove

    • aeneas(rust) = Fast via rank 2 or 3. Fast is already loop- and array-shaped, which makes that refinement

    much easier than one against the clear spec.

4. Trusted base of the refinement proofs (net + beatmap, 2026-10-21)

The Aeneas translation of impl/osu_eval_core (net, beatmap and the POC modules) is checked

against the spec in proofs/OsuProofs. Everything except the lines below is either generated by

Aeneas (Generated/{Types,Funs}.lean), part of the Aeneas library, or proved. The trusted lines are

all in proofs/OsuProofs/Generated/{TypesExternal,FunsExternal}.lean; each is one definition.

Float types. float.F64 := OsuModel.Net.F64 (Float), float.F32 := OsuModel.Net.F32

(Float32). A Rust bit pattern denotes the Lean float with the same bits; every NaN pattern

denotes the model's single NaN.

Float primitives (56, exactly the ones the translation uses). Each float::F64/F32 method is

identified with one OsuModel.Net (or OsuModel.Beatmap.fmodF64) function:

| Rust (float.rs) | Lean meaning | Why it is the same value |

|---|---|---|

| from_bits | Float.ofBits / Float32.ofBits | bit reinterpretation (NaN canonicalised, see above) |

| to_bits (partial: fail on NaN) | toBits | Rust sees the real NaN payload/sign, the model one NaN; proofs must show call sites never pass NaN (the Rust checks is_nan first where NaN can occur: f64_round, f32_round, f64_is_inf, f32_is_inf, decimal::of_f64/of_f32, inverse_sqrt_fast) |

| is_negative (partial) | F64.isNegative | sign bit; meaningful only on non-NaN |

| add sub mul div neg | + - * /, - | IEEE RNE binary64/binary32 (SSE2 = RyuJIT), sign flip |

| lt le eq is_nan | <, ≤, ==, isNaN | IEEE predicates |

| abs floor ceil trunc sqrt | F64.abs/floor/ceiling/truncate/sqrt (F32 likewise) | kernel models, nettest-verified vs .NET (81M + 10M checks) |

| to_f32, F32::to_f64 | F64.toF32, F32.toF64 | cvtsd2ss RNE / exact |

| from_i64, from_u64 (F64, F32) | F64.ofInt, F32.ofInt | one RNE rounding (Rust as) |

| to_i32_sat, to_i64_sat, to_u32, to_u64 (F64; F32 to_i32_sat) | F64.toInt32/toInt64/toUInt32/toUInt64 | Rust as saturates and maps NaN to 0 = .NET 9+ |

| sin cos log atan2 pow … (F64; F32 sin cos atan2 …) | F64.sin … (Lean core @[extern] libm, opaque) | both call glibc 2.39 libm.so.6 (dlopen in Rust) |

| fmod | OsuModel.Beatmap.fmodF64 | IEEE fmod is exact |

| parse_decimal (partial: digits must be 0..9) | ofBitsN (Parse.decToBits fmt neg m e) | Rust dec2flt is correctly rounded; the spec computes the correctly rounded value exactly |

The exact list is the axiom list of Generated/FunsExternal_Template.lean (regenerated with the

translation); FunsExternal.lean defines exactly those names (unused primitives are not defined).

Std items not modelled by the Aeneas library (5). F64/F32::clone (derive(Clone) on a

bit wrapper: identity), Option::<T>::clone, <Option<T> as PartialEq>::eq, Vec::<T>::pop.

Each is defined as the documented std behaviour (pure list/option operations), at the same trust

level as the Aeneas library's own std models.

LZMA (end-to-end evaluator, crate::lzma, 2026-10-22; docs/rust-eval-port.md). One opaque function:

| Rust | Lean meaning | Why it is the same value |

|---|---|---|

| lzma::lzma_alone_decode(input, max_out) -> Result<Vec<u8>, LzmaErr> | OsuModel.Replay.Osr.lzmaAloneDecode (itself an opaque @[extern "osu_lzma_alone_decode"], model/c/lzma_shim.c) | line-by-line port of the C shim onto the same liblzma 5.4.5 (dlopen("liblzma.so.5"); Lean links the static library of the same package); LzmaErr ids = the shim's error strings |

Both the model and the implementation trust liblzma to equal lazer's managed SharpCompress LzmaStream on

well-formed .lzma streams (docs/model-eval.md "Trust boundary").

Not trusted: every .NET semantic (Math.Max/Min/Round/Clamp, decimal, Random, parsing,

BindableNumber, …) is ordinary translated Rust, proved against the spec.

5. Trusted assumptions of the end-to-end theorem (2026-10-22, D35; proofs/OsuProofs/Eval/EndToEnd.lean)

The top-level theorem eval.evaluate_refines holds for inputs satisfying InputBounds bm osr and PlayableBounds bm osr opts (the playable-pipeline size rows below; JsonFinal eval.evaluate_refines_open), and the two named spec-run rows RunBudgetIn / SchedFramesIn (e2e2). The headline is osu_eval_refines (Eval/JsonTop.lean, at default_env; allowlist proofs/scripts/headline_signature.txt).

These are *platform and input-size* hypotheses, not semantic ones: the Rust code panics (overflow / out-of-range

index) beyond them, so the refinement proof needs them; every input lazer accepts is many orders of magnitude below.

They are trusted in the sense that nothing checks them at run time (osu_eval could check the cheap ones up front).

| Hypothesis (InputBounds field) | Required by | Why it is reasonable |

|---|---|---|

| h64 : System.Platform.numBits = 64 | slider_path (D31), schedule/sim2 (usize arithmetic, fuel loops 10^8), decoder (D36) | osu_eval is built and run only on x86-64 Linux (usize = 64 bit). |

| bmLen : .osu bytes < usize::MAX | beatmap.text.stream_reader_decode (D36) | a slice length is ≤ usize::MAX anyway; real .osu files are < 10 MB. |

| decLines: decoded .osu has < 2^31 − 1 lines, every line shorter than N ≤ 2^61, and dec_pathOk N (per hit-object line < 2^32 slider control points, spec calculatePath < 2^62 points) | decoder (D36), hit_object_parser, slider_path of_control_points (D31) | lazer reads lines into C# int-indexed lists (< 2^31); a control point takes ≥ 2 characters, so < 2^32 points is implied by lines < 8 GB; calculatePath emits O(points × bezier subdivisions) vertices, < 2^62 for any file that fits in memory. |

| osrLen : .osr bytes < 2^62 | eval osr/mods_json (D35): reader positions, decompressed text and JSON string lengths (JOk' of mod settings) | LZMA output is bounded by maxPayload = 256 MiB (spec and Rust); real .osr files are < 10 MB. |

| *(derived, not assumed; 2026-10-22 json agent)* LoadBounds.tp/dp/ep/n: decoded timing / difficulty / effect points and hit objects < 2^31 | get_playable_beatmap_refines (via ev_pbOk) | PROVED from decLines (each line adds at most one point / object; the decoder invariant dec_szOk carried to the result: js_decode_sizes, Eval/JsonDecSize.lean; assembled in Eval/JsonPBounds.lean). |

| PlayableBounds.sliderPaths (separate top-level hypothesis PlayableBounds bm osr opts, Eval/E2EBase.lean; = LoadBounds.sl): per decoded slider < 2^32 control points and spec calculatePath (with optimiseCatmull := true) < 2^62 points | get_playable_beatmap_refines (convert_beatmap slider paths) | decLines.dec_pathOk bounds the same quantities for optimiseCatmull := false only; the catmull variant (the D49 control-point rebuild) is polynomial in the line length but not derived. |

| PlayableBounds.decodeTime / .gameplay: GpbBounds D MS for the decode-time mods (bitfield mods without unseeded RD/TP) and for the resolved gameplay mods; conjuncts below | get_playable_beatmap_refines (decode-time check and gameplay playable) | stated on spec values only (no Rust state); not derived (each depends on the per-mod hooks): |

| — GpbBounds.pp: every pre-processed hit object PathsOk | apply_defaults (slider path / cumulative length) | same as sliderPaths, after the AC hooks. |

| — GpbBounds.nest: nested objects per hit object < 2^31 after applyDefaults | apply_defaults (tick / repeat generation) | nested objects = ticks/repeats, capped by lazer's own int indices. |

| — GpbBounds.stk: < 2^62 hit objects, all PathsOk, before stacking | apply_stacking_all | hit-object count is the decoded count (< 2^31). |

| — GpbBounds.atb: before each applyToBeatmap hook: modStates < 2^63, total nested count < 2^31 (asCnt), GenOk for every object, effect / timing lists < 2^31, epoch < 2^63 | apply_to_beatmap (AS, RD, TP generators; gen 119e5d4) | GenOk is the generators' well-formedness of their input objects (RD/TP read existing objects only); the counters are bounded by the number of hooks and objects. |
