| *(no field; D54)* no stack exhaustion: osu_eval runs real_main on a thread with a 4 GiB reserved stack; the recursive JSON readers (eval::mods_json value_f, array_items_rec, object_items_rec) recurse once per nesting level and once per array item / object member, so their depth is bounded by the score-info / --mods JSON size | every refinement theorem through mods_json (score info in osr.decode, parse_mods); Aeneas/Lean model values, not stack usage | measured (release build, 64 MiB test thread): ~161 B of stack per array item, ~178 B per object member, ~369 B per nesting level, i.e. 4 GiB covers ~26M array items, ~24M members or ~11M nesting levels (≥ ~23 MB of JSON text in the worst case, nesting). Real score-info JSON is ~1 KB. NOT implied by InputBounds: osrLen < 2^62 and maxPayload = 256 MiB of decompressed score info admit deeper/wider JSON (DECIDED D57: kept as this trusted row and stated in the Eval/EndToEnd.lean docstring, not as an InputBounds field, since the stackless Aeneas semantics would never use it; --mods JSON is parsed before evaluate, outside its theorem). Beyond the bound the process aborts (stack overflow), it never prints a wrong result. |

| *(no field; final audit M3)* CLI shell impl/osu_eval/src/main.rs (untranslated): argv parsing (option fall-through, schedule names), explicit: file parsing (parse_explicit: trim + double_parse per line), the JSON printer (hex_d, jstr, acr_json, mods_json, sem_json, rejected_line, stage/reason text, playable_json), batch mode; and for --mods: parse_mods yields < 2^61 configs | the headline osu_eval_refines (Eval/JsonTop.lean) is about eval::evaluate; --mods composes via js_hopts_of_parse_mods (every config ev_mcOk, proved from parse_mods_refines) | not translated by Aeneas; evidence is the byte-identical evaltest regressions (D30/D54). Also untranslated (excluded from the eval Charon run with --exclude): the four text modules eval::text, eval::osr::text, eval::mods_json::text, eval::adapter::text (message / name strings); the proofs use ev_tn (Eval/E2EBase.lean), a hand copy of eval::adapter::text::type_name (adapter.rs:289), so that table is trusted to match the Rust one. The 2^61 count: each mod config needs ≥ 2 characters of JSON and the argument is bounded by Linux ARG_MAX (2 MiB), so the count is < 2^20; not proved from the parser. |

| *(no field; final audit M2)* Env.typeNames: OsuModel.Eval.evaluate (ev_envNorm E) = OsuModel.Eval.evaluate E | reading osu_eval_refines at defaultEnv (it is stated at ev_envNorm defaultEnv, which is what eval.env.default_env_refines gives: the Rust Env keeps only an is-PAC flag per chain node) | the spec reads chain-node typeName only in the == "OsuPlayfieldAdjustmentContainer" test of composeChain (Sim/Geometry.lean), which ev_envNorm preserves; not proved (a congruence through the whole sim). Removing the row needs either the invariance proof or making the spec's defaultEnv use "" for non-PAC names (behaviour-preserving, D20c; spec owner). |

| *(no field; final audit m1)* rejection reasons are not compared: ev_topRel relates a Rust rejection to a spec rejection by STAGE only (D52b) | osu_eval_refines, eval.evaluate_refines | the reason text is informational; the printed reason is covered only by the evaltest regressions. |

| *(no field; final audit m2)* floats up to NaN payload: output float fields are compared as Lean Floats; FunsExternal maps every Rust NaN bit pattern to the model's single NaN (§4) | every float field of ev_resS | not proved NaN-free; if a NaN reached an output field, the printed hex_d bits could differ from evaltest's. No NaN output has been observed in the regressions. |

Further size hypotheses of the slice theorems that are discharged *inside* the proof (not trusted), e.g. vector

pushes < usize::MAX that follow from the input bounds, are not listed. Hypotheses found by

grep -rn "numBits\|< 2^6\|< 2^3\|Usize.max" proofs/OsuProofs (2026-10-22): numBits = 64 (93 theorems: sim2 schedule,

slider_path, decoder), < 2^31 (decoder/control-point counts, D33 dec_cpiOk; implied by the line bound), < 2^32

control points (slider_path), < 2^61/2^62 path/line/string sizes (path_approximator, slider_path, number parsing,

D24/D26), < Usize.max slice lengths (D33). Sim-side ones (e.g. refs.len * 10^8 + 4 < 2^61 of

simulate_steps, frame counts) will be added to InputBounds when those theorems are plugged into the

end-to-end proof; until then they appear inside the open EvalAssumptions fields.

Non-size facts the end-to-end theorem assumes (fields of EvalAssumptions, Eval/E2EBase.lean, besides the other

slices' callee theorems), added 2026-10-22 when eval::osr::decode was proved (Eval/Osr.lean):

| Fact | Kind | Why it is reasonable |

|---|---|---|

| lzmaBound (ev_lzmaBound): lzmaAloneDecode d m = .ok r → r.size ≤ m | trusted (LZMA boundary, §4) | the C shim allocates at most maxOut bytes and reports output too large beyond; the Rust port (lzma_alone_decode) is the same code on the same liblzma. Needed because the Rust maps an over-usize::MAX payload to an error. |

| utf8 (ev_utf8Fact): String.fromUTF8? raw = some s → s.toList = decodeUtf8 raw 0 ∧ raw does not start 00 00 FE | PROVED (js_ev_utf8, Eval/JsonUtf8.lean + JsonDischarge.lean) | both are standard UTF-8 decoders; on well-formed input the replacement decoder is the identity, and FE is never valid UTF-8. Only used for the readCompressedText fast path (the Rust always uses decode_utf8). |

| scoreInfo (ev_scoreInfoOk): decode_score_info refines decodeScoreInfo | PROVED under h64 (js_ev_scoreInfo, Eval/JsonScore.lean + JsonSize.lean + JsonDischarge.lean) | ordinary refinement obligation, to be proved. |

5.1 Trusted base of the Rust route (final audit m7, 2026-10-23, infra lead)

Besides the hypotheses above, the end-to-end statement "the osu_eval binary computes what the Lean spec says" rests on

these unchecked parts (none is a hypothesis of a Lean theorem; they are the meta-level link between the theorem and the

running binary):

| Item | Trusted for | Why it is reasonable / how it is checked |

|---|---|---|

| Lean 4.35 kernel (+ core Float as an opaque structure, Mathlib not used by the kernel check) | every theorem | the axiom audit (check_all.sh, #print axioms) shows only propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound; no native_decide/implemented_by/ofReduceBool (final audit §4). |

| Charon (nightly-2026-09-17) + Aeneas translation Rust -> LLBC -> Lean (Generated/{,Sim,Eval}{Types,Funs}.lean) | that the Lean functions are the semantics of impl/osu_eval_core | standard Aeneas trust; freshness of the committed translation is checked mechanically by proofs/scripts/translation_fresh.sh (re-runs the recorded recipes in a window and diffs against Generated/); run 2026-10-23 02:25-02:39: net+beatmap and sim+replay byte-identical, eval identical except the Source: comment paths. |

| Aeneas Std library models (Vec, Slice, scalar arithmetic with overflow = fail, Result) | every Rust primitive the translation calls | part of the Aeneas library (pinned in lake-manifest.json); the 5 hand-written std items are listed in §4. |

| rustc / LLVM code generation (release build of osu_eval) | that the binary runs the Rust semantics Charon saw | standard compiler trust; differential tests (D35 regression runs: Rust binary vs pinned Lean evaltest, byte-identical stdout) are the empirical check. |

| Heap exhaustion aborts the process (Rust alloc failure = abort, never a wrong result) | the Aeneas model treats allocation as total | an out-of-memory run prints nothing / exits non-zero; it can never print a wrong score. |

| Stack: main.rs runs evaluation on a thread with a 4 GiB reserved stack (D57); if that reservation fails it falls back to the default 8 MiB main-thread stack (impl/osu_eval/src/main.rs:623-636), where deep inputs (~200k-item arrays) overflow | recursion depth of the JSON / sim code | stack overflow aborts (guard page), never a wrong result; the 4 GiB reservation is virtual and succeeds on 64-bit Linux in practice. |

| LZMA "out of memory" is nondeterministic in reality but modelled as a deterministic result of the opaque lzmaAloneDecode (§4, ev_lzmaBound) | .osr decoding | the shim reports OOM as an error; the theorem then relates an error to an error. A run that hits OOM can differ from another run of the same input only by failing, never by a different score. |

| Platform: x86-64, glibc 2.39 libm via dlopen, SSE2 (D6) | float primitives (§4) | as documented in §4. |

docs/proof-poc.md

Proof pipeline proof of concept: Rust → Charon → Aeneas → Lean, proved against the spec (D12)

Status (2026-10-21): it works end to end. Three representative Rust functions were translated by

Charon+Aeneas, and each was proved in Lean to refine its OsuModel spec function. The proofs are

machine-checked with no sorry and no new axioms. The only trusted additions are the 18 one-line float

primitive identifications (§3). The same Rust compiles to plain SSE code and agrees with the compiled

Lean spec on random inputs (§6).

Layout:

| Path | What |

|---|---|

| impl/ | Cargo workspace. osu_eval_core (translated) + osu_eval_bench (difftest generator / bench, not translated). |

| impl/charon.sh | Runs Charon, then Aeneas, and writes proofs/OsuProofs/Generated/{Types,Funs}.lean (+ templates). |

| proofs/ | Separate Lean package OsuProofs: requires aeneas (path, release bundle) and OsuModel (../model). |

| proofs/OsuProofs/Generated/ | Aeneas output (Types.lean, Funs.lean, regenerated) + hand-written TypesExternal.lean, FunsExternal.lean (the trusted primitive layer). |

| proofs/OsuProofs/{Prims,HitWindows,Slider,Schedule}.lean | Aeneas-side refinement proofs. |

| proofs/OsuProofs/Spec/{Slider,Schedule}.lean | Spec-side normal forms (import only OsuModel, so they check in ~20 s). |

| proofs/PocSpec/Main.lean | pocspec exe: differential checker using the compiled spec. |

| proofs/scripts/check_all.sh | Fast iteration: concatenates the Aeneas-side proofs into one file, so the slow import is paid once. |

1. Install (exact steps and versions)

Versions:

  • Aeneas release nightly-2026.10.21-fc321a2, asset aeneas-linux-x86_64.tar.gz. It contains its matching charon/charon-driver.
  • Rust nightly-2026-09-17 (rustc 1.100.0-nightly 923c95cdf), minimal profile. Only the rustc component is needed by charon-driver (librustc_driver-*.so); rustc-dev is not.
  • Lean v4.35.0 (already installed) and Mathlib v4.35.0 (rev 56a00585), via a filtered cache.
# a) Aeneas bundle (161 MB download, 517 MB kept)
mkdir -p ~/tools/aeneas && cd ~/tools/aeneas
curl -sL -o /tmp/aeneas.tgz https://github.com/AeneasVerif/aeneas/releases/download/nightly-2026.10.21-fc321a2/aeneas-linux-x86_64.tar.gz
tar xzf /tmp/aeneas.tgz && rm /tmp/aeneas.tgz backends/lean/.lake/lean-build-aeneas-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz
# b) nightly, minimal (602 MB). NEVER let rustup read ~/tools/aeneas/rust-toolchain (adds rustc-dev, miri, 8 targets).
~/.cargo/bin/rustup toolchain install nightly-2026-09-17 --profile minimal
# c) proofs/ package: lakefile.toml requires aeneas (path ~/tools/aeneas/backends/lean) + OsuModel (path ../model).
#    lake-manifest.json is written by hand: the two path deps + aeneas's manifest entries (inherited=true).
#    The git deps are pre-created as SHALLOW clones at the manifest revisions (mathlib clone: 153 MB instead of ~700 MB):
cd ~/lazerproof/proofs/.lake/packages   # for each package in aeneas's lake-manifest.json:
git init -q $name && git -C $name remote add origin $url && git -C $name fetch -q --depth 1 origin $rev && git -C $name checkout -q FETCH_HEAD
# d) filtered Mathlib cache: only the 31 Mathlib modules Aeneas imports (+ their closure: 1474 files, 101 MB of .ltar)
cd ~/lazerproof/proofs
SEEDS=$(grep -rhoE '^(public |meta )*import (all )?Mathlib\S*' ~/tools/aeneas/backends/lean --include=*.lean | sed -E 's/.*import (all )?//' | sort -u)
lake exe cache get- $SEEDS     # download only (builds the `cache` exe once, ~2 min)
lake exe cache get  $SEEDS     # unpack
rm -rf ~/.cache/mathlib proofs/.lake/packages/mathlib/.lake/build/bin   # .ltar copies + the cache exe (216 MB)
# e) 4 Batteries modules that Aeneas imports directly are not in the Mathlib closure; build them (seconds, NOT Mathlib):
lake build Batteries.Data.BitVec.Basic Batteries.Data.Fin.OfBits Batteries.Data.Int Batteries.Data.BitVec.Lemmas
lake build --no-build Aeneas   # must succeed: proves nothing else (Mathlib/Aeneas) needs rebuilding
# f) optional disk saving: delete Mathlib .lean sources that have no .olean (outside the closure): 117 MB -> 17 MB.
#    (lake hashes only the sources of modules it builds or checks.)

Things that did not work or must not be done:

  • Deleting mathlib/.lake/build/ir (the .c files, 137 MB). Aeneas's AeneasMeta uses precompileModules, so lake then wants to rebuild the Mathlib modules in its import chain.
  • Deleting the prebuilt Aeneas ir/ (setup.json + .c) triggers a full rebuild of Aeneas.
  • lake build --no-build <target> is the safe way to check whether lake would compile Mathlib.

Disk and RAM

| Item | Disk |

|---|---|

| ~/tools/aeneas (binaries 86 MB + prebuilt Lean lib 431 MB) | 517 MB |

| ~/.rustup/toolchains/nightly-2026-09-17 (minimal) | 602 MB |

| proofs/.lake (mathlib 1.1 GB incl. 0.9 GB oleans, aesop 134 MB, batteries 82 MB, rest) | 1.4 GB |

| impl/target | 6 MB |

| Total | ≈ 2.5 GB |

Free disk went from 6.7 GB to 4.0 GB at the low point and was 4.5 GB after cleanup.

RAM: import Aeneas maps about 1.2-1.4 GB of oleans (max RSS 1.4 GB, mostly file-backed and reclaimable).

  • Each proof file needed 1.2-2.0 GB RSS.
  • On this VM, under load average 6-12 from the other agents' batches, the import alone took 150-250 s. CPU time was only about 10 s; the rest was page faults.
  • Practical consequences:
  • Build the proofs with -j1, and never next to another Lean/dotnet job.
  • Iterate with scripts/check_all.sh, which pays the import once for all proofs (one round ≈ 4-6 min).
  • Put spec-side lemmas in files that do not import Aeneas (Spec/*.lean check in 5-30 s).

2. Rust crate (impl/osu_eval_core)

| Rust | Spec | Kind |

|---|---|---|

| hit_windows::difficulty_range1/difficulty_range/osu_hit_windows | OsuModel.Beatmap.difficultyRange1/difficultyRange/osuHitWindows | (i) pure numeric |

| hit_windows::result_for | OsuModel.Sim.HitWindows.resultFor | (i) |

| net::{max,min,clamp} | OsuModel.Net.F64.{max,min,clamp} (.NET Math.Max/Min/Clamp) | helpers, *proved*, not trusted |

| slider::cumulative_lengths (+ vsub, length) | OsuModel.Beatmap.SliderPath.calculateLength (no ExpectedDistance) | (ii) loop over a slice, building a Vec |

| schedule::simulate_steps (+ fsc_step, frame_time) | OsuModel.Sim.simulateSteps (FSC + replay handler, D9) | (iii) state machine: nested loops, break, fuel, i64 index, Option |

charon cargo --preset=aeneas --opaque 'crate::float' followed by

aeneas -backend lean -use-lean-modules false -split-files runs in about 5 s.

3. Floats: the trusted primitive layer

impl/osu_eval_core/src/float.rs defines #[repr(transparent)] struct F64(u64) / F32(u32) holding raw bits, with

#[inline(always)] methods.

  • The whole module is opaque to Charon (--opaque crate::float). Aeneas emits axioms only for the

    • primitives that are actually used, in FunsExternal_Template.lean.

  • We replace those with definitions in Generated/TypesExternal.lean and Generated/FunsExternal.lean.
  • The trusted base is exactly these lines:

| Rust primitive | Lean definition (spec function) | Justification |

|---|---|---|

| type F64 / F32 | OsuModel.Net.F64 = Float / F32 = Float32 | bit patterns; every Rust NaN ↦ the model's single NaN |

| F64::from_bits(b) | Float.ofBits b | canonicalises NaN, consistent with the above |

| F64::{add,sub,mul,div} | a + b, a - b, a * b, a / b (Float.Model) | SSE2 addsd… = RyuJIT's; TestFloat-validated model |

| F64::{lt,le,eq} | decide (a < b), decide (a ≤ b), a == b | IEEE predicates |

| F64::is_nan | F64.isNaN | |

| F64::is_negative | if isNaN a then fail .panic else ok (F64.isNegative a) | partial: only identified on non-NaN inputs (Rust sees the real NaN sign bit). The proofs must show that call sites never pass NaN, and net::max/min do show it. |

| F64::abs | F64.abs (clear sign bit) | |

| F64::floor | F64.floor (kernel model, nettest-verified vs .NET) | Rust f64::floor = libm floor or roundsd |

| F64::sqrt | F64.sqrt (kernel model) | sqrtsd |

| F64::to_f32 | F64.toF32 | cvtsd2ss RNE |

| F32::{add,sub,mul} | a + b, a - b, a * b on Float32 | SSE addss… |

| F32::to_f64 | F32.toF64 | exact |

Rules followed by the crate:

  • Every non-trivial .NET semantic (Max/Min/Clamp, …) is written in ordinary Rust over these primitives and proved.
  • Float constants are const K: F64 = F64::from_bits(0x…). Each constant is proved equal to the spec literal by

    • decide +kernel (Lean's float model is kernel-reducible), e.g. CATCHUP_THRESHOLD = sixtyFrameTime * F32.toF64 1.2.

  • To validate the trusted lines, extend model/nettest to call the Rust primitives too. They map to the same instructions, and nettest already checks the Lean models against .NET with 81M cases.

4. Proofs: what is proved, and how much effort it took

Each main theorem is stated as an equation impl … = ok (…spec…). The proofs use the generated

code as is; no annotations were added on the Rust side.

| Theorem (file) | Statement (simplified) | Effort |

|---|---|---|

| difficulty_range_refines, difficulty_range1_refines, osu_hit_windows_refines, result_for_refines (HitWindows.lean) | = ok spec (HitWindows via field-wise map; HitResult via hrSpec) | ~1 h incl. learning; each proof 2-4 lines (unfold; by_cases; simp) |

| max_refines, min_refines, clamp_refines (Prims.lean) | net.max a b = ok (F64.max a b) etc. Needs beq_not_nan_* (IEEE == ⇒ not NaN, proved from Lean's Float.Model) for the partial is_negative | ~30 min |

| cumulative_lengths_refines (Slider.lean + Spec/Slider.lean) | ∃ v, impl path opt = ok (v, sl.calculatedLength) ∧ v.val = sl.cumulativeLength.toList where sl = calculateLength sp (path.map vSpec) opt, sp.expectedDistance = none | ~2 h. Spec side: forIn over [0:n] → List.foldl (core simp lemmas) + List.foldl_hom. Impl side: induction on the remaining length; bounds by omega |

| simulate_steps_refines (Schedule.lean + Spec/Schedule.lean) | ∃ v, impl refs frames gst = ok v ∧ v.val.map stepSpec = simulateSteps refs frames gst under numBits = 64 and refs.length * 10^8 + 4 < 2^61 | ~4 h. Spec side: while+break → structural recursion inner (via Lean.Loop.forIn_eq_of_monadTail, Lean ≥ 4.3x) + Array.forIn_pure_yield_eq_foldl. Impl side: fsc_step by case split, then inner/outer loop inductions with the invariant |idx| ≤ 1 + steps.length |

How loops, overflow and panics show up

  • Loops. Aeneas turns every Rust while into loop body state, where body : state → Result (ControlFlow state result) and

    • loop is a partial_fixpoint. So there is no termination proof at translation time; *total correctness is proved* by our induction.

  • Nested loops become separate …_loop0_loop0 functions.
  • The inner break is done.
  • We prove a one-line unfolding lemma per loop (cum_loop_unfold etc.) that keeps the recursive call folded. If you simp with the body equation directly, it also unfolds the body under the loop binder and later rws fail.
  • Overflow and panics. Every + - on usize/i64/u32, every slice index and every Vec::push is a Result that fails on

    • overflow or out-of-bounds (Vec.push fails at Usize.max).

  • Each refinement theorem therefore *proves absence of panics*, under explicit size hypotheses.
  • The scalar-arith lemmas come from Aeneas (I64.add_spec, …). We wrap them as equations (i64_add_one, usize_add_one, push_eq, index_eq in Prims.lean) and discharge their side conditions with omega.
  • Platform. Usize.max is platform-abstract (32 or 64 bit), so i as usize and large Vecs need the hypothesis System.Platform.numBits = 64.
  • The spec's fuel. simulateSteps loops at most 10^8 times per reference. The Rust copies that bound exactly (FUEL: u32). The theorem needs refs.length * 10^8 < 2^61 only so that the counters provably cannot overflow.

5. Friction points (and the fix used)

  • Field named ok (HitWindows.ok) breaks the generated Lean: inside the struct's namespace ok self resolves to the field

    • projection. We renamed the Rust field to ok_. Rule: never name Rust fields or functions ok, fail, div, loop, bind.

  • The module system. Aeneas emits module files by default, and module files cannot import the non-module OsuModel.

    • Use -use-lean-modules false.

  • Name resolution in FunsExternal. Inside def float.F64.abs, the name F64.abs resolves to itself. Write OsuModel.Net.F64.abs.
  • no_std. f64::floor/sqrt need std, so the crate is std (+ alloc::vec::Vec).
  • Result is an interaction tree (coinductive). cases works through its custom eliminator (ret/vis/div). bind_ok simp lemmas are

    • available, but simp does not push ok through if, so we add ite_ok (Prims.lean).

  • Derives. derive(Debug, PartialEq) generate a lot of translated noise (fmt, discriminant compare). Derive only Clone, Copy.
  • Prop vs Bool. if a.lt(b) becomes if decide (a < b) = true. simp normalises it, but the spec's && of Bools versus Rust's

    • short-circuit && (nested if) needs a case split (repeat' split; simp_all). That is fine for about 10 branches.

  • Do-notation shape of the spec (Lean 4.35's new do elaborator).
  • Mutable state is a nested *tuple* (not MProd).
  • The continuation after an if is *duplicated* into each branch, so simulateSteps' loop body is a large if-tree.
  • It was matched against our compact stepT by case splitting on first/manual<gst/…, then repeat' split; all_goals simp_all (30 s).
  • generalize of subterms breaks this (dependent Decidable instances), so don't.
  • Slice.length/Vec.length are abbrevs that omega treats as atoms different from s.val.length. Always state bounds with .val.length.
  • Iteration speed (§1). This was the dominant cost.

6. Runtime: native float code and differential test

  • Assembly (RUSTFLAGS="--emit asm", release):
  • Every wrapper op is a single SSE instruction. F64(u64) lives in an xmm register; from_bits/to_bits vanish.
  • cumulative_lengths inner loop: subss/mulss/addss → sqrtss → cvtss2sd → addsd. LLVM legally replaced

    • (float)Math.Sqrt((double)x) by sqrtss, which is bit-identical for binary32.

  • osu_hit_windows even vectorises two lanes (mulpd/addpd, the same IEEE ops per lane).
  • With the default x86-64 baseline target, floor is a call to glibc floor (no SSE4.1). With -C target-cpu=native it becomes roundsd. Both are exact.
  • Benchmark (osu_eval_bench bench, under load average ≈10, so noisy):

| Operation | Time |

|---|---|

| result_for (1M calls) | ~20 ns/call |

| cumulative_lengths | 11-19 ns/point |

| Same loop written with plain f32/f64 | 12-18 ns/point (no measurable wrapper cost) |

| simulate_steps (100k perframe refs) | 10-45 ns/step |

  • Differential test against the compiled Lean spec: see the last section ("Results").

7. Recommendation: scaling to the whole evaluator

Verdict: D12's Aeneas route is viable on this VM.

  • Install footprint ≈ 2.5 GB, as estimated.
  • Translation is instant.
  • Proof effort is roughly 1 h per 10-20 lines of Rust after the learning curve, dominated by loop invariants and by matching the spec's control-flow shape.

The real risk is iteration latency (minutes per check) on a loaded 2-core VM, not expressiveness.

Plan

  • Write the Rust impl function-by-function mirroring the spec (same decomposition, same operation order). Every spec def gets a Rust fn and a

    • *_refines theorem stated as impl … = ok (repr (spec …)).

  • Spec-side normal forms first. For each spec loop, prove in an Aeneas-free file that the do/for/while code equals a plain

    • recursion or fold. Reuse the generic loop_inner/forIn_yield lemmas from Spec/Schedule.lean. These checks are fast, and they are where most

    spec-shape surprises show up.

  • Generic loop library. Factor the three loop proofs into reusable lemmas:
  • "Aeneas index loop over a slice = List.foldl";
  • "fuel loop with break = inner";
  • "Vec.push accumulation = List.append".

    • Most evaluator loops have one of these shapes.

  • Representation maps live in one file: impl struct ↦ spec struct (field-wise), i64.val, Vec.val.toArray, enums by match.

    • Prefer making Rust structs field-for-field identical to the spec records.

  • CI: charon.sh && lake build OsuProofs (≈ 15-25 min on this VM), plus the pocspec-style difftest for every ported function.

Rust style rules (to keep translation and proofs tractable)

  • Floats only through float::{F64,F32} methods. No f64 in translated code, no operator traits (a.add(b), not a + b).

    • Constants: const K: F64 = F64::from_bits(0x…), each with a decide +kernel lemma.

  • Never add a new opaque primitive casually. Each one is trusted and must be one IEEE operation equal to an existing OsuModel.Net function, and it should be added to nettest. Anything with .NET logic is written in translated Rust.
  • Partial primitives (meaningless on NaN, etc.) get fail outside their domain in FunsExternal.
  • Control flow:
  • while loops with an explicit index or fuel counter;
  • no iterators/closures (for x in v.iter(), map), no return/break out of nested loops, no ? on custom error types;
  • Option for .NET exceptions.
  • Mirror the spec's branch structure where it is cheap. Put the "compute" part in a small non-looping fn (like fsc_step), so that the

    • loop proof only needs that fn's refinement lemma.

  • Integers: usize indices, i64 only where the spec has Int. Keep the bounds needed for no-overflow derivable from one global size

    • hypothesis (e.g. number of frames/objects < 2^31).

  • Structs: plain struct with named fields, #[derive(Clone, Copy)] at most.
  • No field or fn named ok, fail, div, loop, bind, cont, done.
  • No trait objects, no generics instantiated with &mut, no unsafe.
  • Vec only for append-only outputs and read-only inputs (&[T]). For in-place state updates, prefer returning a new state struct (as with

    • SimState) over &mut borrows into collections. Aeneas supports &mut, but the proof terms get heavier.

  • Keep each translated fn small, at most ~40 lines and at most one loop. Case-split proofs scale with the branch count of a single function.

Results (2026-10-21)

  • lake build OsuProofs succeeds: all theorems in §4 are proved with no sorry. OsuProofs/Axioms.lean prints the axioms of

    • each main theorem (confirmed: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound only). There is no native_decide.

  • Differential test: impl/target/release/osu_eval_bench gen N SEED | proofs/.lake/build/bin/pocspec (spec-only exe,

    • lake build pocspec).

| Run | Cases | Mismatches |

|---|---|---|

| gen 200000 42 | 200k | 0 |

| gen 1000000 7 | 1M | 0 |

  • The cases are spread evenly over 4 kinds: hit windows + resultFor, difficultyRange on raw/special doubles, slider lengths on random

    • f32 paths incl. NaN/∞/subnormal bits, and step schedules with out-of-order frames.

  • NaNs compare equal to any NaN.
  • The generator keeps references and frame times finite. With a NaN reference, proposed == r never holds, so spec *and* impl run the

    • full 10^8-step fuel per reference (≈3 GB; earlyoom killed it). That is a spec property, not a mismatch.

  • Run the generator under ulimit -v, but not the Lean exe: the Lean runtime aborts under ulimit -v.
  • Build command, honouring the STATE.md resource rule: LEAN_NUM_THREADS=1 tools/heavy lake build OsuProofs pocspec (≈15-20 min incl.

    • regenerated files). If model/ switches lakefile format (it moved from lakefile.toml to lakefile.lean), update configFile in

    proofs/lake-manifest.json.

docs/proof-status.md

Refinement proof status (generated by proofs/scripts/proof_status.py)

Categories (D44): proved = unconditional, against the real spec def (the only ones counted); CONDITIONAL = assumes another refinement (hypotheses listed; tag -- CONDITIONAL: ... or auto-detected = ok/_refines/EvalAssumptions hypotheses); FRAGMENT = against a local copy of a spec body (tag -- FRAGMENT-OF: ...). Done = 0 CONDITIONAL and 0 FRAGMENT.

COVERED (D63) = no own proof, but every Rust call site lies inside a proved (or covered) fn; not counted as proved; the end-to-end finish line uses proved + covered.

net+beatmap: 559/559 Rust functions proved to refine their spec def, covered 0 (0 more CONDITIONAL, 0 FRAGMENT) (impl x = ok (spec x) or the guarded form in the theorem docstring); axioms checked by proofs/scripts/check_all.sh (#print axioms). Constants, loop helpers and derive boilerplate are not counted (constants are covered inside the proofs that use them; loops by their function's theorem).

docs/rust-eval-port.md

Rust port of the end-to-end model (OsuModel.Eval) and osu_eval

impl/osu_eval_core/src/eval/* ports the Lean end-to-end layer function by function (Aeneas subset,

impl/STYLE.md, "Translatability" in docs/rust-sim-port.md); impl/osu_eval is a drop-in for the Lean

evaltest (same CLI, byte-identical stdout). With the Net/Beatmap port (net, beatmap) and the Sim port

(sim, replay) this gives a Rust path .osu + .osr (+ mods) + schedule → result. DECISIONS D18.

Correspondence (spec = Lean at 1b0a176)

| Lean | Rust |

|---|---|

| Eval.lean (Schedule, Options, Rejection, Result, sameMods, unseededRandom, resolveMods, playableOf, evaluate, playableFor) | eval/mod.rs (EvalResult = Result without the unused playable field) |

| Eval/Adapter.lean (toSimPlayable, judgementOf, …) | eval/adapter.rs; the Dump section (playableJson) is in the shell osu_eval/src/main.rs |

| Eval/Env.lean (defaultEnv, incl. the HOC ancestor chains of 95499c3; #guard chainsConsistent) | eval/env.rs (+ unit test chains_consistent) |

| Replay/Osr.lean | eval/osr.rs |

| Sim/ModsJson.lean (SimJson.V, value, toSetting, parseMods) | eval/mods_json.rs |

| lzmaAloneDecode (@[extern], model/c/lzma_shim.c) | lzma.rs — trusted, opaque to Charon |

| EvalTest/Main.lean | osu_eval/src/main.rs (not translated) |

Representation choices:

  • The reader monad RdM = ReaderT ByteArray (StateT Nat (Except String)) → (b: &[u8], p: usize) -> Result<(T, usize), OsrErr>;

    • the JSON parser StateT (List Char) (Except String) → (s: &[u32], p) -> Result<(V, usize), JsonErr> (the remaining

    list = s[p..]; the spec's list recursion in strBody is a loop).

  • Spec String messages → error enums with payloads (OsrErr, JsonErr, ModsJsonErr, eval::Reason,

    • eval::Stage); the exact texts are in untranslated text submodules and osu_eval (sim messages as in simtest_rs).

  • HObj.typeName : String → type_id constants adapter::T_* (text table adapter::text::type_name).
  • String.toNat! / Int range checks (toSetting, jsonInt): magnitude saturated at 2^64 in u128 (only compared

    • against 64-bit ranges). String.isNat/toInt? follow Lean 4.35 (_ digit separators allowed between digits).

  • readCompressedText's fast path (String.fromUTF8? on BOM-less input) → utf8_valid + decode_utf8.
  • Printing: Lean's Float.toBits canonicalises NaN (verified on the 4.35 runtime), so osu_eval prints

    • NaNs as 0x7ff8000000000000 / 0x7fc00000. JSON strings use Lean.Json.escape's rules.

  • Not ported: playableOverride / --sim-playable (localisation only). osu_eval --batch LIST (lines

    • BEATMAP OSR OUT [MODS-JSON]) is an addition for throughput.

Trust boundary: LZMA

crate::lzma::lzma_alone_decode is a line-by-line port of osu_lzma_alone_decode (same initial buffer size,

growth, 256 MiB bound and lzma_ret → message mapping) onto the same system liblzma (xz-utils 5.4.5), resolved with

dlopen("liblzma.so.5")/dlsym (as float.rs resolves libm): no build script and no new link dependency for the

other workspace binaries. See docs/proof-pipeline.md §4 (trusted base).

Translatability (Charon + Aeneas)

`OUT=<scratch> HEAVY_MIN_MEM_MB=3000 tools/heavy impl/charon_check.sh --start-from crate::eval --opaque crate::lzma

--exclude crate::eval::text --exclude crate::eval::osr::text --exclude crate::eval::mods_json::text --exclude

code it calls) with 0 errors and 0 sorry (bdcbd22+: Funs.lean 2.3 MB, ~2,360 definitions, 280 of them eval.*).

Peak RSS 2.7–2.9 GB, 3–5 min — it fits a normal heavy slot (no HEAVY_EXCLUSIVE needed). Opaque items: the 57 float

primitives, lzma.lzma_alone_decode (the one new trusted item), and the std models already in the trusted base

(Option::clone, Option::eq, Vec::pop). The generated Lean is not yet type-checked against the proofs package.

Fixes needed (rule already in impl/STYLE.md §5, "update loop state unconditionally"): a loop whose only state change is

a conditional r = true / r = Some(i) on a test of a borrowed slice element (find_first, has_autoplay,

stats_entries_ok) → "Could not match the contexts"; written as r = r || test(xs, i) /

r = first_match(test(xs, i), i) with the test in a helper taking the slice and the index. A derive(PartialEq) on an

enum of the opaque lzma module becomes one more axiom: LzmaErr/OsrErr derive only Clone, Copy.

A run with --opaque on beatmap/sim/net (to translate eval alone) does not work: field accesses of opaque structs fail.

docs/rust-sim-port.md

Rust port of the Sim model (M0-M7, total)

impl/osu_eval_core/src/sim/* and impl/osu_eval_core/src/replay/* port the Lean simulation model

function by function, in the Aeneas subset (docs/proof-poc.md style rules, impl/STYLE.md). impl/simtest_rs is a

drop-in for the Lean simtest (same CLI and byte-identical JSON output).

Pinned spec (ported incrementally)

| Rust commit | Lean spec commit | scope |

|---|---|---|

| 6da616b … 43ae79c | 3f88501 | M0-M4 core + NF/CL |

| c949ed3 (tag rust-sim-m56) | 3f88501 | + M5/M6 sim-side mods (all of that spec's Config.ofMods, AutoGen) |

| f0f6889 (verified: 6,540/6,540) | 7cffd29 | + M7: transform engine (Sim/Transforms.lean → sim/transforms.rs), pooled DHO instances, presence-gated subtree updates, slider body refresh (G1), rotation geometry, GR/DF/SI/TP/TR/WG/HD/CL-early-fade handlers, DP/MG/RP/BR, spinner-tick DHOs, per-judgement ReplayPlayer fields in the output |

| 5afe1a5 (verified: 2,980/2,980) | 171dd71 | + Autopilot's injected MouseMove also sets cursorPos (read by MG/RP in the same P3) |

| f3cc2a1 (verified: 10,492/10,492) | e0e8215 | total simulation (G17): rejections as Result<_, SimErr> (section "Totality") |

Each step is verified against a Lean simtest built from the pinned commit in a separate worktree (copy of

model/.lake, then lake build simtest). Next diffs: git diff e0e8215 -- model/OsuModel/Sim model/OsuModel/Replay model/SimTest.

MG/RP are ported from the fixed magnetUpdate (e4d512b: the hoisted headIdx lookup for circles), never from a panicking

version; rust_sim_diff.py reports any Lean PANIC on stderr.

Scope

All sim-side behaviour of the pinned spec: replay frame decode, FSC schedules, input/hover, float32 hit-test matrices

(now from each pooled DHO instance's current placement), lifetimes/alive dictionary order, hit policies, circles,

sliders, spinners, score + health processors with both fail semantics, and every mod Config.ofMods handles

(mods come as beatmap::mod_settings::ModConfig, i.e. the Beatmap port's APIMod.ToMod). Debug-only spec options

(--trace-obj, --dbg-no-presence, --trace-tracking, --print-geom, --check-env, the dbg stderr lines) are not

ported.

Totality (Lean G17, e0e8215; DECISIONS D16)

The spec's SimM = ReaderT Ctx (StateT St (Except String)) becomes (c: &Ctx, s: &mut St) -> Result<T, SimErr>

(sim/err.rs); Except-returning pure spec functions (references, simulateSteps, steps, sliderGeom,

bodyRefresh, positionAt, curvePositionAt, isMouseInFollowArea, HealthSt.drain, computeDrainRate,

computeLegacyDrainRate, mkHealthCfg, AutoGen.*, timeRampRate, DynRate.setSpeed/initialSpeed,

inputBlockPeriods, mkCtx, initState, runWith, simulate) return Result too (NetExn-valued where the

spec is Except NetExn). A Rust function returns Result iff some spec rejection is reachable through it; the rest

keep their plain signatures.

  • SimErr has one variant per spec throw site (lazer would throw: … with the NetExn, malformed …, fuel

    • exhaustion, and the non-index internal: ones). simtest_rs renders the spec's exact message

    ({"error":"sim: …"}, exit 1; Lean Float toString = %f/NaN/inf, repr of Kind/NetExn).

  • getA/setA/need on arrays whose size is a simulation invariant (objs, insts, nested, pools,

    • headIdx, asSeen, …) stay plain indexing: a violation is a Rust panic (Aeneas fail), unreachable, and a run

    whose spec result is .ok performs the same in-range accesses. sliderData/need … "slider data" is

    Internal::MissingSliderData.

  • Evaluation order of rejections follows the spec: mkCtx = AutoGen, steps, health config, input-block periods,

    • preceding end times, slider heads (all objects), slider tails; then initState (AS bindables, then every dynamic

    rate's initial speed); then the run.

  • crate::schedule (the proof-POC simulate_steps, proven against the pre-G17 proofs/OsuProofs/Spec/Schedule.lean)

    • is unchanged; the sim uses sim::schedule::simulate_steps, which rejects on Math.Clamp with out-of-order frame

    times and on fuel exhaustion.

  • Former silent defaults that are now rejections: exOr on AS clamps/Math.Sign/Average, TimeRamp rate

    • rounding, bindable setters; slider.getD default; a missing alive-dictionary entry on becameDead; the

    HandleHit depth bound; the ComputeDrainRate/legacy/ReportDelta/bonus-score fuel; empty slider path and short

    cumulative_length; inverted drain bounds; Math.Sign(NaN); invalid input-block periods. The playable loader

    rejects an odd number of path coordinates and breaks that are not [start, end].

Correspondence

Every Lean def has a Rust fn with the snake_case name and a doc comment naming it; loops with break/early

return are split into small helper fns (e.g. enumerate_up_to + push_nested_up_to, drain_pass,

legacy_pass, lifetime_first_update / lifetime_future_update). SimM := ReaderT Ctx (StateM St) becomes

(c: &Ctx, s: &mut St).

| Lean | Rust |

|---|---|

| Sim/Basic.lean | sim/basic.rs (+ sim/netx.rs: F64.round/sign/copySign, F32.max/min/clamp/sign, Bindable.equalsD) |

Representation choices (all bijective on reachable states):

  • HObj.typeName : String → type_id: u32 into a name table held by the shell.
  • statistics Array Nat (100 entries by enum value) → [u64; 18] by ordinal (hr_index).
  • action lists (List Action / Array Action, at most 3 distinct elements) → ActList { items: [Action; 3], len }.
  • freeList : List Nat (head = most recently freed) → Vec with the head at the end.
  • receptorCornerRadiusPow (closed term) → computed once into Ctx.corner_pow.
  • Int.emod (spanAt p) 2 == 1 → span_at(p) % 2 != 0 (odd test, also for negative spans).

Trusted primitives added to float.rs (additive)

F64::{trunc, pow (glibc pow), from_i64, from_u64, to_i32_sat, to_i64_sat, parse_decimal},

F32::{neg, le, is_nan, is_negative, abs, pow (powf), atan2 (atan2f), from_i64, to_i32_sat, parse_decimal}.

parse_decimal(neg, digits, exp10) = Parse.decToBits (correctly rounded decimal → binary, via Rust's dec2flt,

which is correctly rounded for any input length; exponent beyond ±65536 with > 65536 digits is the only theoretical

divergence).

Translatability (Charon + Aeneas)

2026-10-21, total sim (Lean e0e8215 port), 8 GB VM: `HEAVY_EXCLUSIVE=1 OUT=… tools/heavy impl/charon_check.sh

--start-from crate::sim --start-from crate::replay (Aeneas -sequential`) translates every sim/replay function

with 0 errors and 0 sorry (Funs.lean 1.3 MB, 1338 definitions incl. loop bodies and the reachable net/beatmap

dependencies; 51 opaque float primitives). Peak RSS 2.6 GB, 6 min wall. The generated Lean is not yet type-checked

against the proofs package. Fixes needed for the Result port (rules for later diffs):

  • An early exit (? or return) inside a loop is translated only when the loop is not nested in a branch of a

    • surrounding if/match, and no early exit precedes it in the function (the rest of a function after an early

    return/? becomes a nested branch in LLBC). So: every loop that can reject is the first statement of its own

    helper function (initial values as parameters; return the loop state, e.g. the remaining fuel, and do post-loop

    checks in the caller): move_frames, spinner_frames, slider_frames, bonus_spins, handle_hit_sto,

    generate_objects, as_init/initial_speeds; one-iteration bodies with several ? are helpers too

    (move_frame_step, spinner_frame_step, slider_frame_step, bonus_spin, break_block_period).

    Otherwise "Early returns inside of loops are not supported yet" / "Breaks to outer loops are not supported yet".

  • let x = if k == Head { slider_data(c, i)?.classic } else { false } (a ? on a borrowing call inside a

    • value-returning if) → "Could not match the contexts": move the if into a helper (is_classic_head,

    depth_slider_duration).

  • Indexing a global constant array of byte-string pairs (COMBOS[ci]) → "Unimplemented"; a match returning the

    • literals → "There should be no bottoms in the value". Unrolled calls with literal arguments (apply_combo) work.

  • v[i] = x + 1 after a ? (index assignment with an arithmetic right-hand side) → "Unimplemented binary operation";

    • bind the value to a local first (small-crate test).

Earlier (M0-M4 only, 2-core VM):

charon cargo --preset=aeneas --opaque crate::float --start-from crate::sim --start-from crate::replay followed by

aeneas -backend lean -split-files translates all 414 sim/replay functions without errors (generated Lean not yet

type-checked against the proofs package). Translating the whole crate at once needs ~3 GB RSS in charon-driver

(earlyoom kills it on this VM), hence the per-module --start-from.

Aeneas failures found and fixed (rules to follow when porting later Lean diffs):

  • A local shared borrow created *before* a loop and used inside it (let o = &s.objs[i]; while … o.nested[k] …)

    • → "Could not match the contexts". Index directly in the loop or move the loop into a helper fn that takes the

    reference as a parameter (os_all_judged, push_simulated, max_end_time, legacy_nested_loop, …).

    The same error appears on a value-returning if chain while borrows from slider_data(c, i) are live

    (slider_result helper).

  • match slice[i] { Variant { field, .. } => …, _ => {} } → "Not allowed to expand enumerations with several variants":

    • match on &slice[i] in a helper with all variants listed (classic_health_of, is_no_fail).

  • A loop that only conditionally overwrites a usize accumulator with a by-value param comparison

    • (last_idx_of_kind) → "Could not compute a loop fixed point": accumulate into an Option from a copied field.

  • return inside a while + Vec index assignment (trigger_failure) → "Unimplemented binary operation": use a

    • stop flag.
